It was said: what is meant is Jibril alone, and he is mentioned with the plural form to honour him, although he is not without followers among the angels. Qatadah said: what is meant is everyone who recites the remembrance of Allah and His books.

It was said: what is meant is the verses of the Qur'an, and describing them as recited even though they are recited (by others), as in His saying: ﴿This Qur'an narrates to the Children of Israel﴾ [al-Naml: 76]. It was also said: because some of them recite after others and follow them.

Al-Mawardi mentioned that al-talayat are the prophets, reciting the remembrance to their nations. The accusative of "dhikran" is as a direct object, and it may also be a verbal noun like what precedes it in "saffan, zajran".

It was said: this fa' in "fa-al-zajirat, fa-al-talayat" is either for the ordering of the attributes themselves in existence, or for the ordering of their described referents in merit. Both views are open to consideration.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, your God is one﴾ is the answer to the oath, meaning: Allah swore by these oaths that He is One, having no partner. Al-Kisa'i permitted opening the inna that occurs as the answer to an oath.

﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth﴾ may be a second predicate, or a substitute for "la-wahid", or the predicate of an omitted subject.

Ibn al-Anbari said: stopping at "la-wahid" is a good pause, and then one begins "Lord of the heavens and the earth" with the meaning "He is the Lord of the heavens and the earth."

Al-Nahhas said: it may also be a substitute for "la-wahid".

The meaning in the verse: the existence of these creatures in this wondrous form is among the clearest proofs of the existence and power of the Creator, and that He is the Lord of all that, that is, its Creator and Owner.

By "what is between them" is meant the created beings between the heavens and the earth.

By ﴿the easts﴾ is meant the risings of the sun. It was said: Allah – glory be to Him – created for the sun each day a rising point and a setting point, according to the number of days of the year; it rises each day from one of them and sets from one of them. Thus said Ibn al-Anbari and Ibn 'Abd al-Barr.

As for His saying in Surat al-Rahman ﴿Lord of the two easts and Lord of the two wests﴾ [al-Rahman: 17], by "the two easts" is meant the farthest point of rising in the long days and the shortest day in the short days, and likewise for "the two wests".

As for mentioning "the east" and "the west" in the singular, what is meant is the direction from which the sun rises and the direction in which it sets. Perhaps a fuller discussion of this has already preceded us.

﴿Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with an adornment of the stars﴾. By "the nearest heaven" is meant the one nearest the earth, from proximity (dunuww), which is nearness; it is the closest of the heavens to the earth.

The majority read "bi-zinati al-kawakib" with "zinat" in construct with "al-kawakib". The meaning: We adorned it with the beautifying of the stars, that is, with their beauty.

Masruq, al-A'mash, al-Nakha'i, and Hamzah read "zinatin" with tanwin and "al-kawakib" in the genitive, as a substitute (badal) for the adornment, the adornment being understood as a noun rather than a verbal noun. The construction after dropping the substituted-for noun is: We adorned the heaven with the stars, for the stars in themselves are a great adornment, since to the eyes of those who look at them they are like shining jewels.

'Asim, in the narration of Abu Bakr from him, read "zinatin" with tanwin and "al-kawakib" in the accusative, the adornment being a verbal noun whose agent is omitted; the meaning: that Allah adorned the stars by their being luminous and beautiful in themselves. Or the stars may be in the accusative by an implied "a'ni" (I mean), or as a substitute for "al-sama'" (the heaven) as a substitution of inclusion (badal ishtimal). The accusative of "hifzan" is as a verbal noun with an implied verb, meaning: We guarded it with a guarding; or as an object of purpose, meaning: We adorned it with the stars for protection; or by coordination with the position of "zinatin", as if He said: We created the stars as an adornment for the heaven.

﴿And as protection from every rebellious devil﴾: meaning, one who is defiant, outside obedience, who is pelted with the stars, as in His saying: ﴿And We have certainly adorned the nearest heaven with lamps and made them missiles against the devils﴾ [al-Mulk: 5].

The clause ﴿They cannot listen to the exalted assembly﴾ is a resumed sentence explaining their state after the heaven has been guarded against them.

Abu Hatim said: meaning, "so that they do not hear"; then he deleted "an" and so raised the verb. Al-Kalbi said likewise. The "exalted assembly" (al-mala' al-a'la) are the people of the nearest heaven and what is above it; all of them are called "exalted" by their being attributed to the assembly of the earth. The pronoun in "yassamma'una" refers to the devils.

It was said: the clause "la yassamma'una" is a description of "every devil". It was said: it is an answer to an implied question, as if it were said: "What was their state after the heaven was guarded against them?" and so He said: ﴿They cannot listen to the exalted assembly﴾. The majority read "yasma'una" with a sukun on the sin and lightening of the mim. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and 'Asim in the narration of Hafs from him read with doubling of the mim and the sin, the original being "yatasamma'una", with the ta' assimilated into the sin. The first reading indicates the negation of their hearing, without their listening; the second indicates the negation of both. In the sense of the first reading is His saying: ﴿Indeed, they are removed from hearing﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 212]. Mujahid said: "They used to eavesdrop, but they would not hear."

Abu 'Ubaydah preferred the second reading, saying: "Because the Arabs hardly say sami'tu ilayhi (I listened to him), but they say tasamma'tu ilayhi (I eavesdropped to him)."

﴿And they are pelted from every side, repelled﴾: meaning, they are struck from every side of the sky's sides with shooting stars when they try to ascend to steal hearing. The accusative of "duhuran" is as an object of purpose. Duhur means repelling; one says "dahartuhu dahran wa duhuran": I drove him away.

The majority read "duhuran" with a damma on the dal. 'Ali, al-Sulami, Ya'qub al-Hadrami, and Ibn Abi 'Ablah read it with a fatha.

It is narrated from Abu 'Amr that he read "yaqdhifun" in the active voice, but this reading does not conform to what is intended by the Qur'anic wording. It was said: the accusative of "duhuran" is as a circumstantial state (hal), meaning "madhurin" (repelled). It was said: it is the plural of "dahir", like "qa'id" and "qu'ud", and so it is also a state. It was said: it is a verbal noun of an implied verb, meaning "yudhharun duhuran" (they are repelled with repelling).

Al-Farra' said: the meaning is "they are pelted with what repels them", that is, with a repelling; then the preposition was deleted and the word became accusative by removal of the preposition.

It has been disputed whether this pelting of them with shooting stars occurred before the mission (al-mab'ath) or after it. Some said the former, others the latter. Another group said both are combined: the devils were not pelted before the mission with pelting that cut them off from hearing, but they were pelted at some times and not at others, and from one side and not from another. Then after the mission they were pelted at every time and from every side, until they were no longer able to steal any of the hearing except one who snatched a snatch, and a piercing flame followed him. The meaning of ﴿and for them is a perpetual punishment﴾ is: for them is a lasting punishment that does not cease, and what is meant is the punishment in the Hereafter, other than the punishment they receive in this world from the pelting with shooting stars.

Muqatil said: "that is, perpetual until the first blast." The first is preferable.

The majority of the exegetes held that al-wasib means the lasting. Al-Suddi, Abu Salih, and al-Kalbi said: it is the painful, whose pain reaches the heart, derived from al-wasab, which is sickness. It was said: it is the severe.

The exception in His saying ﴿except one who snatches a snatch﴾ is either from His saying ﴿they cannot listen﴾ or from His saying ﴿and they are pelted﴾.

It was said: the exception refers to other than revelation, given His saying ﴿Indeed, they are removed from hearing﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 212]; rather, one of them snatches a snatch of what the angels discuss among themselves and what will occur in the world before the people of the earth know it.

Al-Khatf is stealing by stealth and taking something quickly.

The majority read ﴿khatifa﴾ with a fatha on the kha' and a kasra on the ta', lightened. Qatadah and al-Hasan read with kasra on both and doubling of the ta'; this is the dialect of Tamim ibn Murr and Bakr ibn Wa'il. 'Isa ibn 'Umar read with a fatha on the kha' and a kasra on the ta' doubled. Ibn 'Abbas read with kasra on both and lightening of the ta'.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 37, verses 1–19 (part 2 of 2):

It has also been said that the exception (in ﴿except one who snatches a fragment﴾) is disjunctive (munqati'). ﴿Then a piercing flame pursued him﴾: that is, a piercing flame (shihab thaqib) overtook him and followed him. It is a shining star that burns him. Sometimes it does not burn him, and he throws what he snatched to his companions. The meteors with which the (devils) are pelted are not from the fixed stars but from other than the fixed stars. The root meaning of thuqub is brightness.

Al-Kisa'i said: "thaqabat al-nar yathqubu thaqabatan wa thuquban" means the fire blazed up. This verse is like His saying: ﴿except one who snatches a hearing, then a clear flame pursues him﴾ [al-Hijr: 18].

﴿So ask them: are they stronger in creation, or those whom We have created?﴾ That is: ask the disbelievers who deny the Resurrection whether they are stronger in creation, mightier in bodies and greater in limbs, or those whom We created, from the heavens and the earth and the angels? Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is: ask them a question of reproof (su'al taqrir): "Are they stronger in creation," that is, more perfect in workmanship, "or those whom We created before them from the earlier nations?" He means: they are not stronger in creation than the other nations, and We destroyed them for their denial, so what secures them from punishment? Then He mentioned the creation of man, saying: ﴿Indeed We created them from clay that adheres﴾. That is: indeed We created them, within the creation of their father Adam, from clay that adheres (lazib), that is, sticky. It is said: "lazaba yalzubu luzuban" means it clung. Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said: al-lazib is that which sticks. Ikrimah said: al-lazib is the sticky (lazij). Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: al-lazib is the good clay that clings to the hand. Mujahid said: it is al-lazim (the firm, constant), and the Arabs say: "tin lazib" and "tin lazim," substituting the "ba'" for the "mim." Al-lazim is that which is fixed, as it is said: "the matter became a lasting blow" (darbat lazib). From this is the saying of al-Nabighah:

Do not think good is without any evil after it,
nor think that evil is a lasting blow.

Al-Farra' related from the Arabs: "tin latib," meaning lazim, and al-latib is the fixed. Al-Asma'i said: al-latib is the adhering, like al-lazib.

The meaning of the verse is: how do these people find the Return far-fetched, when they were created from this weak creation, and yet one who was created with a creation stronger, greater, more complete and more perfect than theirs did not deny it? It has also been said: al-lazib is the foul-smelling (al-muntin), said by Mujahid and al-Dahhak.

Al-Jumhur (the majority of readers) read ﴿am man khalaqna﴾ with a shaddah on the mim, and it is the connective am (am al-muttasilah). Al-A'mash read it with a light (unshaddah) mim, and in his reading it is a second interrogative.

It has been said: "lazim" and "latib" have also been read (as variants), but I do not know who read that.

Then He (glorified is He) turned away from the previous speech and said: ﴿Rather, you (O Muhammad) are amazed﴾ at the power of Allah (glorified is He), ﴿and they mock﴾ you because of your amazement, or they mock you for what you say about affirming the Return.

Al-Jumhur read ﴿'ajibta﴾ with a fatha on the ta', in address to the Prophet (ﷺ). Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read it with a damma, and this reading was transmitted from Ali, Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas, and was chosen by Abu Ubayd and al-Farra'.

Al-Farra' said: the people read it with a fatha and a damma on the ta', and the damma is more beloved to me, because it is transmitted from Ali, Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) and Ibn Abbas.

He said: "The attribution of 'ajab (amazement) to Allah: its meaning from Allah is not like its meaning from the servants."

Al-Harawi said: some of the imams said: the meaning of His saying ﴿Rather, you are amazed﴾ is: rather, He recompensed them for their amazement, because Allah reported about them in more than one place their amazement at the creation, as He said: ﴿And they wondered that a warner from among them came to them﴾ [Sad: 4], and they said: ﴿Indeed this is a strange thing﴾ [Sad: 5], and ﴿Is it a marvel for the people that We revealed to a man from among them?﴾ [Yunus: 2].

Ali ibn Sulayman said: the meaning of the two readings is one, and the estimate is: "Say, O Muhammad, rather I am amazed," because the Prophet (ﷺ) is addressed by the Qur'an. Al-Nahhas said: this is a good view, and the omission of "say" (idmar al-qawl) is common.

It has also been said: the meaning of Allah's report about Himself with amazement is that there appeared from His command and His wrath upon those who disbelieved in Him something that stands in the place of amazement from creatures.

Al-Harawi said: it is said: the meaning of "'ajiba rabbukum" is: your Lord was pleased and rewarded, so He called it amazement, though it is not amazement in reality. So the meaning of "'ajibta" here is: their action was great in my sight. Al-Naqqash related that the meaning of "bal 'ajibta" is: rather, you denied (anka rta). Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: amazement from Allah is the denial of a thing and its magnification, and this is the language of the Arabs. It has also been said: its meaning is that He reached, in the completeness of His power and the abundance of His creatures, a point at which He was amazed by them, while these people, out of their ignorance, mock them. The waw in ﴿wa yaskhurun﴾ is for the state (hal), that is: rather you are amazed while they are mocking, and it may be for resumption (isti'naf).

﴿And when they are reminded, they do not remember﴾: that is, when they are admonished with an admonition from the admonitions of Allah or the admonitions of His Messenger, they do not remember, that is, they are not admonished by them and do not benefit from what is in them.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: that is, when they are told what befell the deniers among those before them, they turn away from it and do not reflect.

﴿And when they see a sign﴾: that is, a miracle from the miracles of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), ﴿they mock greatly﴾: that is, they exaggerate in mockery.

Qatadah said: they mock and say that it is mockery. It is said: "sakhira" and "istaskhara" have the same meaning, like "qarra" and "istaqarra," and "'ajiba" and "ista'jaba." The first (sakhira) is preferable, because the increase in the form indicates an increase in meaning.

It has also been said: the meaning of "yastaskhirun" is: they seek mockery from others. Mujahid said: they ridicule.

﴿And they say: this is nothing but manifest magic﴾: that is, what this is that you bring to us is nothing but clear, evident magic.

﴿When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be raised?﴾ The interrogative is for denial, that is: shall we be raised when we have died? The governing element of "idha" is what is indicated by ﴿shall we indeed be raised (a-innaa lamab'uthun)﴾, which is "a-nub'athu," since the one who is raised (mab'uthun) is not (the one who governs it), because of the intervention of what prevents its action in it. This denial of the Resurrection by them is the reason for which they denied the messengers and what was sent down to them, and mocked what they brought of miracles. The meaning of this verse has already been explained in several places.

﴿Or our forefathers, the earlier ones?﴾ It is a subject (mubtada') whose predicate is omitted, that is: "or our forefathers, the earlier ones, shall be raised?" It has been said: it is coordinated with the place (mahall) of "inna" and its noun. It has also been said: it is coordinated with the pronoun in "mab'uthun," because of the separation between them. The hamzah is for denial and enters upon the conjunction particle. For this reason al-Jumhur read it with a fatha on the waw, while Ibn 'Amir and Qalun read it with a sukun on it, on the basis that "aw" is the coordinating particle and the hamzah is not interrogative.

Then Allah (glorified is He) commanded His Messenger to answer on their behalf as a rebuke to them, saying: ﴿Say: yes, and you will be humbled﴾: that is, yes, you will be raised, and you will be abject and humiliated.

Al-Wahidi said: "al-dukhur" is the most severe of humiliation. The clause ﴿and you are humbled (wa antum dakhirun)﴾ is in the place of an accusative as a state (hal).

Then He (glorified is He) mentioned that their raising will occur with a single cry, saying: ﴿It will be but one shout﴾. The pronoun refers to the matter (al-qissah) or to the raising (al-ba'thah) understood from what precedes it, that is: the matter of the raising, or the raising, is but one shout, that is, one cry from Israfil by his blowing into the Trumpet at the Resurrection. ﴿Then behold, they will be looking﴾: that is, they will see what Allah does to them of punishment.

Al-Hasan said: it is the second blast. The cry was called "zajrah" because its purpose is rebuke (zajr). It has also been said: the meaning of "yanzurun" is "yantazirun," that is, they await what will be done to them. The first is preferable.

Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, and al-Hakim, who declared it sound, related through several chains from Ibn Mas'ud regarding ﴿By those who line up in rows﴾: he said: the angels. ﴿By those who drive with a driving﴾: he said: the angels. ﴿By those who recite a reminder﴾: he said: the angels.

Abd ibn Humayd related the same from Mujahid and Ikrimah. Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh in al-Azhamah related the same from Ibn Abbas.

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh related from him that he used to read ﴿they cannot listen to the exalted assembly﴾ with a light (mukhaffafah) sin, and said: they used to listen stealthily, but they could not listen.

Ibn Jarir related from him also, regarding His saying ﴿a perpetual punishment (adhab wasib)﴾: he said: lasting.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh in al-Azhamah related from him also: ﴿so a piercing flame pursued him﴾.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from him also regarding ﴿so a piercing flame pursued him﴾: he said: they are not killed by the flame and they do not die. But they are burned, injured and wounded, without being killed.

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him also regarding His saying ﴿from clay that adheres (min tin lazib)﴾: he said: sticking.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn al-Mundhir related from him also ﴿from clay that adheres﴾: he said: the sticky, good (clay).

Ibn Abi Hatim related from him also: he said: al-lazib, al-hama' (black mud) and al-tin are one: its beginning was dust, then it became foul-smelling black mud, then it became adhesive clay, and Allah created Adam from it.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Mas'ud: he said: al-lazib is that which sticks some of it to others.

Al-Firyabi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Hakim, who declared it sound, related from Ibn Mas'ud that he used to read ﴿Rather, you are amazed, and they mock﴾ with a damma on the ta' of "'ajibtu" (i.e., ﴿'ajibtu﴾, the speaker being Allah).

Tafsir of Surah al-Saffat

It is Meccan. Al-Qurtubi said: this is the consensus. Ibn al-Duraysi, Ibn al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "It was revealed in Makkah."

Al-Nasa'i and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated from Ibn 'Umar that he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to instruct us to be brief, and he would lead us in prayer with al-Saffat." Ibn Kathir said: al-Nasa'i alone narrated it.

Ibn Abi Dawud in Fada'il al-Qur'an, and Ibn al-Najjar in his History, narrated through the route of Nahshal ibn Sa'id al-Wardani, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Ya-Sin and al-Saffat on Friday and then asks Allah, He will give him what he asks for."

Abu Nu'aym in al-Dala'il, and al-Silafi in al-Tuyuriyyat, narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "When the kings of Hadramawt asked the Prophet (ﷺ), upon their arrival to him, to recite to them something of what Allah had revealed, he recited ﴿By those ranged in ranks﴾ until he reached ﴿and Lord of the easts﴾" [i.e., the Surah of al-Saffat] — the hadith.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

His saying: ﴿By those ranged in ranks﴾. Abu 'Amr, Hamzah, and it was said: Hamzah alone, read with idgham (assimilation) of the ta' of al-Saffat into the sad of saffan, and the idgham of the ta' of al-Zajirat into the zay of zajran, and the idgham of the ta' of al-Talayat into the dhal of dhikran. This reading was rejected by Ahmad ibn Hanbal when he heard it.

Al-Nahhas said: It is far-fetched in Arabic from three aspects. The first: the ta' is not from the articulation point of the sad, nor of the zay, nor of the dal, nor of their cognates.

The second: the ta' is in one word and what follows it is in another word.

The third: when you assimilate, you bring together two sakin (unvowelled) letters from two words, and bringing together two sakin letters in such a case is only permissible when they are in one word.

Al-Wahidi said: The idgham of the ta' into the sad is good because the two letters are close in articulation, for do you not see that both are from the tip of the tongue?

The rest read with clear pronunciation (idhar) of all of that. The waw is for oath, and the one sworn by is the angels: "those ranged in ranks" (al-saffat), "those who drive" (al-zajirat), and "those who recite" (al-talayat). The meaning of "al-saffat" is those that are arranged in rows in the heavens among the angels, like the rows of creation in this world. This was said by Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, and Qatadah.

It was also said: they arrange their wings in the air, standing in it until Allah commands them with what He wills.

Al-Hasan said: "in ranks" like their rows before their Lord in their prayer.

It was said: the meaning of al-saffat here is birds, as in His saying: ﴿Have they not seen the birds above them, spreading their wings?﴾ [al-Mulk: 19].

The first is preferable. And al-saff (the row) is the arrangement of a group along a line, like the row in prayer.

It was said: al-saffat are the groups of believing people when they stand in rows in prayer or in jihad; this was mentioned by al-Qushayri.

By "al-zajirat" is meant the angels who perform zajr (driving), either because they drive the clouds, as al-Suddi said, or because they drive from sins through admonitions and advice.

Qatadah said: by "al-zajirat" is meant the admonitions of the Qur'an, which is everything that forbids and drives away from evil. The first is preferable.

The accusative of ﴿saffan﴾ and ﴿zajran﴾ is as verbal nouns (masdar) to emphasise what precedes them.

It was said: by "al-zajirat" is meant the scholars, because they are the ones who drive away the people of sin. Zajr originally means pushing with force, and here it means the force of vocal shouting; from it is the poet's saying:

"The driving of Abu 'Urwah the beasts of prey when he feared they would mix with the sheep"

And from it: "I drove the camels and sheep" when you frightened them with your voice.

By ﴿then those who recite the remembrance﴾ is meant the angels who recite the Qur'an, as Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan, Mujahid, Ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi said.

It was said: what is meant is Jibril alone, and he is mentioned with the plural form to honour him, although he is not without followers among the angels. Qatadah said: what is meant is everyone who recites the remembrance of Allah and His books.

It was said: what is meant is the verses of the Qur'an, and describing them as recited even though they are recited (by others), as in His saying: ﴿This Qur'an narrates to the Children of Israel﴾ [al-Naml: 76]. It was also said: because some of them recite after others and follow them.

Al-Mawardi mentioned that al-talayat are the prophets, reciting the remembrance to their nations. The accusative of "dhikran" is as a direct object, and it may also be a verbal noun like what precedes it in "saffan, zajran".

It was said: this fa' in "fa-al-zajirat, fa-al-talayat" is either for the ordering of the attributes themselves in existence, or for the ordering of their described referents in merit. Both views are open to consideration.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, your God is one﴾ is the answer to the oath, meaning: Allah swore by these oaths that He is One, having no partner. Al-Kisa'i permitted opening the inna that occurs as the answer to an oath.

﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth﴾ may be a second predicate, or a substitute for "la-wahid", or the predicate of an omitted subject.

Ibn al-Anbari said: stopping at "la-wahid" is a good pause, and then one begins "Lord of the heavens and the earth" with the meaning "He is the Lord of the heavens and the earth."

Al-Nahhas said: it may also be a substitute for "la-wahid".

The meaning in the verse: the existence of these creatures in this wondrous form is among the clearest proofs of the existence and power of the Creator, and that He is the Lord of all that, that is, its Creator and Owner.

By "what is between them" is meant the created beings between the heavens and the earth.

By ﴿the easts﴾ is meant the risings of the sun. It was said: Allah – glory be to Him – created for the sun each day a rising point and a setting point, according to the number of days of the year; it rises each day from one of them and sets from one of them. Thus said Ibn al-Anbari and Ibn 'Abd al-Barr.

As for His saying in Surat al-Rahman ﴿Lord of the two easts and Lord of the two wests﴾ [al-Rahman: 17], by "the two easts" is meant the farthest point of rising in the long days and the shortest day in the short days, and likewise for "the two wests".

As for mentioning "the east" and "the west" in the singular, what is meant is the direction from which the sun rises and the direction in which it sets. Perhaps a fuller discussion of this has already preceded us.

﴿Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with an adornment of the stars﴾. By "the nearest heaven" is meant the one nearest the earth, from proximity (dunuww), which is nearness; it is the closest of the heavens to the earth.

The majority read "bi-zinati al-kawakib" with "zinat" in construct with "al-kawakib". The meaning: We adorned it with the beautifying of the stars, that is, with their beauty.

Masruq, al-A'mash, al-Nakha'i, and Hamzah read "zinatin" with tanwin and "al-kawakib" in the genitive, as a substitute (badal) for the adornment, the adornment being understood as a noun rather than a verbal noun. The construction after dropping the substituted-for noun is: We adorned the heaven with the stars, for the stars in themselves are a great adornment, since to the eyes of those who look at them they are like shining jewels.

'Asim, in the narration of Abu Bakr from him, read "zinatin" with tanwin and "al-kawakib" in the accusative, the adornment being a verbal noun whose agent is omitted; the meaning: that Allah adorned the stars by their being luminous and beautiful in themselves. Or the stars may be in the accusative by an implied "a'ni" (I mean), or as a substitute for "al-sama'" (the heaven) as a substitution of inclusion (badal ishtimal). The accusative of "hifzan" is as a verbal noun with an implied verb, meaning: We guarded it with a guarding; or as an object of purpose, meaning: We adorned it with the stars for protection; or by coordination with the position of "zinatin", as if He said: We created the stars as an adornment for the heaven.

﴿And as protection from every rebellious devil﴾: meaning, one who is defiant, outside obedience, who is pelted with the stars, as in His saying: ﴿And We have certainly adorned the nearest heaven with lamps and made them missiles against the devils﴾ [al-Mulk: 5].

The clause ﴿They cannot listen to the exalted assembly﴾ is a resumed sentence explaining their state after the heaven has been guarded against them.

Abu Hatim said: meaning, "so that they do not hear"; then he deleted "an" and so raised the verb. Al-Kalbi said likewise. The "exalted assembly" (al-mala' al-a'la) are the people of the nearest heaven and what is above it; all of them are called "exalted" by their being attributed to the assembly of the earth. The pronoun in "yassamma'una" refers to the devils.

It was said: the clause "la yassamma'una" is a description of "every devil". It was said: it is an answer to an implied question, as if it were said: "What was their state after the heaven was guarded against them?" and so He said: ﴿They cannot listen to the exalted assembly﴾. The majority read "yasma'una" with a sukun on the sin and lightening of the mim. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and 'Asim in the narration of Hafs from him read with doubling of the mim and the sin, the original being "yatasamma'una", with the ta' assimilated into the sin. The first reading indicates the negation of their hearing, without their listening; the second indicates the negation of both. In the sense of the first reading is His saying: ﴿Indeed, they are removed from hearing﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 212]. Mujahid said: "They used to eavesdrop, but they would not hear."

Abu 'Ubaydah preferred the second reading, saying: "Because the Arabs hardly say sami'tu ilayhi (I listened to him), but they say tasamma'tu ilayhi (I eavesdropped to him)."

﴿And they are pelted from every side, repelled﴾: meaning, they are struck from every side of the sky's sides with shooting stars when they try to ascend to steal hearing. The accusative of "duhuran" is as an object of purpose. Duhur means repelling; one says "dahartuhu dahran wa duhuran": I drove him away.

The majority read "duhuran" with a damma on the dal. 'Ali, al-Sulami, Ya'qub al-Hadrami, and Ibn Abi 'Ablah read it with a fatha.

It is narrated from Abu 'Amr that he read "yaqdhifun" in the active voice, but this reading does not conform to what is intended by the Qur'anic wording. It was said: the accusative of "duhuran" is as a circumstantial state (hal), meaning "madhurin" (repelled). It was said: it is the plural of "dahir", like "qa'id" and "qu'ud", and so it is also a state. It was said: it is a verbal noun of an implied verb, meaning "yudhharun duhuran" (they are repelled with repelling).

Al-Farra' said: the meaning is "they are pelted with what repels them", that is, with a repelling; then the preposition was deleted and the word became accusative by removal of the preposition.

It has been disputed whether this pelting of them with shooting stars occurred before the mission (al-mab'ath) or after it. Some said the former, others the latter. Another group said both are combined: the devils were not pelted before the mission with pelting that cut them off from hearing, but they were pelted at some times and not at others, and from one side and not from another. Then after the mission they were pelted at every time and from every side, until they were no longer able to steal any of the hearing except one who snatched a snatch, and a piercing flame followed him. The meaning of ﴿and for them is a perpetual punishment﴾ is: for them is a lasting punishment that does not cease, and what is meant is the punishment in the Hereafter, other than the punishment they receive in this world from the pelting with shooting stars.

Muqatil said: "that is, perpetual until the first blast." The first is preferable.

The majority of the exegetes held that al-wasib means the lasting. Al-Suddi, Abu Salih, and al-Kalbi said: it is the painful, whose pain reaches the heart, derived from al-wasab, which is sickness. It was said: it is the severe.

The exception in His saying ﴿except one who snatches a snatch﴾ is either from His saying ﴿they cannot listen﴾ or from His saying ﴿and they are pelted﴾.

It was said: the exception refers to other than revelation, given His saying ﴿Indeed, they are removed from hearing﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 212]; rather, one of them snatches a snatch of what the angels discuss among themselves and what will occur in the world before the people of the earth know it.

Al-Khatf is stealing by stealth and taking something quickly.

The majority read ﴿khatifa﴾ with a fatha on the kha' and a kasra on the ta', lightened. Qatadah and al-Hasan read with kasra on both and doubling of the ta'; this is the dialect of Tamim ibn Murr and Bakr ibn Wa'il. 'Isa ibn 'Umar read with a fatha on the kha' and a kasra on the ta' doubled. Ibn 'Abbas read with kasra on both and lightening of the ta'.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 37, verses 1–19 (part 2 of 2):

It has also been said that the exception (in ﴿except one who snatches a fragment﴾) is disjunctive (munqati'). ﴿Then a piercing flame pursued him﴾: that is, a piercing flame (shihab thaqib) overtook him and followed him. It is a shining star that burns him. Sometimes it does not burn him, and he throws what he snatched to his companions. The meteors with which the (devils) are pelted are not from the fixed stars but from other than the fixed stars. The root meaning of thuqub is brightness.

Al-Kisa'i said: "thaqabat al-nar yathqubu thaqabatan wa thuquban" means the fire blazed up. This verse is like His saying: ﴿except one who snatches a hearing, then a clear flame pursues him﴾ [al-Hijr: 18].

﴿So ask them: are they stronger in creation, or those whom We have created?﴾ That is: ask the disbelievers who deny the Resurrection whether they are stronger in creation, mightier in bodies and greater in limbs, or those whom We created, from the heavens and the earth and the angels? Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is: ask them a question of reproof (su'al taqrir): "Are they stronger in creation," that is, more perfect in workmanship, "or those whom We created before them from the earlier nations?" He means: they are not stronger in creation than the other nations, and We destroyed them for their denial, so what secures them from punishment? Then He mentioned the creation of man, saying: ﴿Indeed We created them from clay that adheres﴾. That is: indeed We created them, within the creation of their father Adam, from clay that adheres (lazib), that is, sticky. It is said: "lazaba yalzubu luzuban" means it clung. Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said: al-lazib is that which sticks. Ikrimah said: al-lazib is the sticky (lazij). Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: al-lazib is the good clay that clings to the hand. Mujahid said: it is al-lazim (the firm, constant), and the Arabs say: "tin lazib" and "tin lazim," substituting the "ba'" for the "mim." Al-lazim is that which is fixed, as it is said: "the matter became a lasting blow" (darbat lazib). From this is the saying of al-Nabighah:

Do not think good is without any evil after it,
nor think that evil is a lasting blow.

Al-Farra' related from the Arabs: "tin latib," meaning lazim, and al-latib is the fixed. Al-Asma'i said: al-latib is the adhering, like al-lazib.

The meaning of the verse is: how do these people find the Return far-fetched, when they were created from this weak creation, and yet one who was created with a creation stronger, greater, more complete and more perfect than theirs did not deny it? It has also been said: al-lazib is the foul-smelling (al-muntin), said by Mujahid and al-Dahhak.

Al-Jumhur (the majority of readers) read ﴿am man khalaqna﴾ with a shaddah on the mim, and it is the connective am (am al-muttasilah). Al-A'mash read it with a light (unshaddah) mim, and in his reading it is a second interrogative.

It has been said: "lazim" and "latib" have also been read (as variants), but I do not know who read that.

Then He (glorified is He) turned away from the previous speech and said: ﴿Rather, you (O Muhammad) are amazed﴾ at the power of Allah (glorified is He), ﴿and they mock﴾ you because of your amazement, or they mock you for what you say about affirming the Return.

Al-Jumhur read ﴿'ajibta﴾ with a fatha on the ta', in address to the Prophet (ﷺ). Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read it with a damma, and this reading was transmitted from Ali, Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas, and was chosen by Abu Ubayd and al-Farra'.

Al-Farra' said: the people read it with a fatha and a damma on the ta', and the damma is more beloved to me, because it is transmitted from Ali, Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) and Ibn Abbas.

He said: "The attribution of 'ajab (amazement) to Allah: its meaning from Allah is not like its meaning from the servants."

Al-Harawi said: some of the imams said: the meaning of His saying ﴿Rather, you are amazed﴾ is: rather, He recompensed them for their amazement, because Allah reported about them in more than one place their amazement at the creation, as He said: ﴿And they wondered that a warner from among them came to them﴾ [Sad: 4], and they said: ﴿Indeed this is a strange thing﴾ [Sad: 5], and ﴿Is it a marvel for the people that We revealed to a man from among them?﴾ [Yunus: 2].

Ali ibn Sulayman said: the meaning of the two readings is one, and the estimate is: "Say, O Muhammad, rather I am amazed," because the Prophet (ﷺ) is addressed by the Qur'an. Al-Nahhas said: this is a good view, and the omission of "say" (idmar al-qawl) is common.

It has also been said: the meaning of Allah's report about Himself with amazement is that there appeared from His command and His wrath upon those who disbelieved in Him something that stands in the place of amazement from creatures.

Al-Harawi said: it is said: the meaning of "'ajiba rabbukum" is: your Lord was pleased and rewarded, so He called it amazement, though it is not amazement in reality. So the meaning of "'ajibta" here is: their action was great in my sight. Al-Naqqash related that the meaning of "bal 'ajibta" is: rather, you denied (anka rta). Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: amazement from Allah is the denial of a thing and its magnification, and this is the language of the Arabs. It has also been said: its meaning is that He reached, in the completeness of His power and the abundance of His creatures, a point at which He was amazed by them, while these people, out of their ignorance, mock them. The waw in ﴿wa yaskhurun﴾ is for the state (hal), that is: rather you are amazed while they are mocking, and it may be for resumption (isti'naf).

﴿And when they are reminded, they do not remember﴾: that is, when they are admonished with an admonition from the admonitions of Allah or the admonitions of His Messenger, they do not remember, that is, they are not admonished by them and do not benefit from what is in them.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: that is, when they are told what befell the deniers among those before them, they turn away from it and do not reflect.

﴿And when they see a sign﴾: that is, a miracle from the miracles of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), ﴿they mock greatly﴾: that is, they exaggerate in mockery.

Qatadah said: they mock and say that it is mockery. It is said: "sakhira" and "istaskhara" have the same meaning, like "qarra" and "istaqarra," and "'ajiba" and "ista'jaba." The first (sakhira) is preferable, because the increase in the form indicates an increase in meaning.

It has also been said: the meaning of "yastaskhirun" is: they seek mockery from others. Mujahid said: they ridicule.

﴿And they say: this is nothing but manifest magic﴾: that is, what this is that you bring to us is nothing but clear, evident magic.

﴿When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be raised?﴾ The interrogative is for denial, that is: shall we be raised when we have died? The governing element of "idha" is what is indicated by ﴿shall we indeed be raised (a-innaa lamab'uthun)﴾, which is "a-nub'athu," since the one who is raised (mab'uthun) is not (the one who governs it), because of the intervention of what prevents its action in it. This denial of the Resurrection by them is the reason for which they denied the messengers and what was sent down to them, and mocked what they brought of miracles. The meaning of this verse has already been explained in several places.

﴿Or our forefathers, the earlier ones?﴾ It is a subject (mubtada') whose predicate is omitted, that is: "or our forefathers, the earlier ones, shall be raised?" It has been said: it is coordinated with the place (mahall) of "inna" and its noun. It has also been said: it is coordinated with the pronoun in "mab'uthun," because of the separation between them. The hamzah is for denial and enters upon the conjunction particle. For this reason al-Jumhur read it with a fatha on the waw, while Ibn 'Amir and Qalun read it with a sukun on it, on the basis that "aw" is the coordinating particle and the hamzah is not interrogative.

Then Allah (glorified is He) commanded His Messenger to answer on their behalf as a rebuke to them, saying: ﴿Say: yes, and you will be humbled﴾: that is, yes, you will be raised, and you will be abject and humiliated.

Al-Wahidi said: "al-dukhur" is the most severe of humiliation. The clause ﴿and you are humbled (wa antum dakhirun)﴾ is in the place of an accusative as a state (hal).

Then He (glorified is He) mentioned that their raising will occur with a single cry, saying: ﴿It will be but one shout﴾. The pronoun refers to the matter (al-qissah) or to the raising (al-ba'thah) understood from what precedes it, that is: the matter of the raising, or the raising, is but one shout, that is, one cry from Israfil by his blowing into the Trumpet at the Resurrection. ﴿Then behold, they will be looking﴾: that is, they will see what Allah does to them of punishment.

Al-Hasan said: it is the second blast. The cry was called "zajrah" because its purpose is rebuke (zajr). It has also been said: the meaning of "yanzurun" is "yantazirun," that is, they await what will be done to them. The first is preferable.

Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, and al-Hakim, who declared it sound, related through several chains from Ibn Mas'ud regarding ﴿By those who line up in rows﴾: he said: the angels. ﴿By those who drive with a driving﴾: he said: the angels. ﴿By those who recite a reminder﴾: he said: the angels.

Abd ibn Humayd related the same from Mujahid and Ikrimah. Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh in al-Azhamah related the same from Ibn Abbas.

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh related from him that he used to read ﴿they cannot listen to the exalted assembly﴾ with a light (mukhaffafah) sin, and said: they used to listen stealthily, but they could not listen.

Ibn Jarir related from him also, regarding His saying ﴿a perpetual punishment (adhab wasib)﴾: he said: lasting.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh in al-Azhamah related from him also: ﴿so a piercing flame pursued him﴾.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from him also regarding ﴿so a piercing flame pursued him﴾: he said: they are not killed by the flame and they do not die. But they are burned, injured and wounded, without being killed.

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him also regarding His saying ﴿from clay that adheres (min tin lazib)﴾: he said: sticking.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn al-Mundhir related from him also ﴿from clay that adheres﴾: he said: the sticky, good (clay).

Ibn Abi Hatim related from him also: he said: al-lazib, al-hama' (black mud) and al-tin are one: its beginning was dust, then it became foul-smelling black mud, then it became adhesive clay, and Allah created Adam from it.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Mas'ud: he said: al-lazib is that which sticks some of it to others.

Al-Firyabi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Hakim, who declared it sound, related from Ibn Mas'ud that he used to read ﴿Rather, you are amazed, and they mock﴾ with a damma on the ta' of "'ajibtu" (i.e., ﴿'ajibtu﴾, the speaker being Allah).

Tafsir of Surah al-Saffat

It is Meccan. Al-Qurtubi said: this is the consensus. Ibn al-Duraysi, Ibn al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "It was revealed in Makkah."

Al-Nasa'i and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated from Ibn 'Umar that he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to instruct us to be brief, and he would lead us in prayer with al-Saffat." Ibn Kathir said: al-Nasa'i alone narrated it.

Ibn Abi Dawud in Fada'il al-Qur'an, and Ibn al-Najjar in his History, narrated through the route of Nahshal ibn Sa'id al-Wardani, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Ya-Sin and al-Saffat on Friday and then asks Allah, He will give him what he asks for."

Abu Nu'aym in al-Dala'il, and al-Silafi in al-Tuyuriyyat, narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "When the kings of Hadramawt asked the Prophet (ﷺ), upon their arrival to him, to recite to them something of what Allah had revealed, he recited ﴿By those ranged in ranks﴾ until he reached ﴿and Lord of the easts﴾" [i.e., the Surah of al-Saffat] — the hadith.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

His saying: ﴿By those ranged in ranks﴾. Abu 'Amr, Hamzah, and it was said: Hamzah alone, read with idgham (assimilation) of the ta' of al-Saffat into the sad of saffan, and the idgham of the ta' of al-Zajirat into the zay of zajran, and the idgham of the ta' of al-Talayat into the dhal of dhikran. This reading was rejected by Ahmad ibn Hanbal when he heard it.

Al-Nahhas said: It is far-fetched in Arabic from three aspects. The first: the ta' is not from the articulation point of the sad, nor of the zay, nor of the dal, nor of their cognates.

The second: the ta' is in one word and what follows it is in another word.

The third: when you assimilate, you bring together two sakin (unvowelled) letters from two words, and bringing together two sakin letters in such a case is only permissible when they are in one word.

Al-Wahidi said: The idgham of the ta' into the sad is good because the two letters are close in articulation, for do you not see that both are from the tip of the tongue?

The rest read with clear pronunciation (idhar) of all of that. The waw is for oath, and the one sworn by is the angels: "those ranged in ranks" (al-saffat), "those who drive" (al-zajirat), and "those who recite" (al-talayat). The meaning of "al-saffat" is those that are arranged in rows in the heavens among the angels, like the rows of creation in this world. This was said by Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, and Qatadah.

It was also said: they arrange their wings in the air, standing in it until Allah commands them with what He wills.

Al-Hasan said: "in ranks" like their rows before their Lord in their prayer.

It was said: the meaning of al-saffat here is birds, as in His saying: ﴿Have they not seen the birds above them, spreading their wings?﴾ [al-Mulk: 19].

The first is preferable. And al-saff (the row) is the arrangement of a group along a line, like the row in prayer.

It was said: al-saffat are the groups of believing people when they stand in rows in prayer or in jihad; this was mentioned by al-Qushayri.

By "al-zajirat" is meant the angels who perform zajr (driving), either because they drive the clouds, as al-Suddi said, or because they drive from sins through admonitions and advice.

Qatadah said: by "al-zajirat" is meant the admonitions of the Qur'an, which is everything that forbids and drives away from evil. The first is preferable.

The accusative of ﴿saffan﴾ and ﴿zajran﴾ is as verbal nouns (masdar) to emphasise what precedes them.

It was said: by "al-zajirat" is meant the scholars, because they are the ones who drive away the people of sin. Zajr originally means pushing with force, and here it means the force of vocal shouting; from it is the poet's saying:

"The driving of Abu 'Urwah the beasts of prey when he feared they would mix with the sheep"

And from it: "I drove the camels and sheep" when you frightened them with your voice.

By ﴿then those who recite the remembrance﴾ is meant the angels who recite the Qur'an, as Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan, Mujahid, Ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi said.

It was said: what is meant is Jibril alone, and he is mentioned with the plural form to honour him, although he is not without followers among the angels. Qatadah said: what is meant is everyone who recites the remembrance of Allah and His books.

It was said: what is meant is the verses of the Qur'an, and describing them as recited even though they are recited (by others), as in His saying: ﴿This Qur'an narrates to the Children of Israel﴾ [al-Naml: 76]. It was also said: because some of them recite after others and follow them.

Al-Mawardi mentioned that al-talayat are the prophets, reciting the remembrance to their nations. The accusative of "dhikran" is as a direct object, and it may also be a verbal noun like what precedes it in "saffan, zajran".

It was said: this fa' in "fa-al-zajirat, fa-al-talayat" is either for the ordering of the attributes themselves in existence, or for the ordering of their described referents in merit. Both views are open to consideration.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, your God is one﴾ is the answer to the oath, meaning: Allah swore by these oaths that He is One, having no partner. Al-Kisa'i permitted opening the inna that occurs as the answer to an oath.

﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth﴾ may be a second predicate, or a substitute for "la-wahid", or the predicate of an omitted subject.

Ibn al-Anbari said: stopping at "la-wahid" is a good pause, and then one begins "Lord of the heavens and the earth" with the meaning "He is the Lord of the heavens and the earth."

Al-Nahhas said: it may also be a substitute for "la-wahid".

The meaning in the verse: the existence of these creatures in this wondrous form is among the clearest proofs of the existence and power of the Creator, and that He is the Lord of all that, that is, its Creator and Owner.

By "what is between them" is meant the created beings between the heavens and the earth.

By ﴿the easts﴾ is meant the risings of the sun. It was said: Allah – glory be to Him – created for the sun each day a rising point and a setting point, according to the number of days of the year; it rises each day from one of them and sets from one of them. Thus said Ibn al-Anbari and Ibn 'Abd al-Barr.

As for His saying in Surat al-Rahman ﴿Lord of the two easts and Lord of the two wests﴾ [al-Rahman: 17], by "the two easts" is meant the farthest point of rising in the long days and the shortest day in the short days, and likewise for "the two wests".

As for mentioning "the east" and "the west" in the singular, what is meant is the direction from which the sun rises and the direction in which it sets. Perhaps a fuller discussion of this has already preceded us.

﴿Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with an adornment of the stars﴾. By "the nearest heaven" is meant the one nearest the earth, from proximity (dunuww), which is nearness; it is the closest of the heavens to the earth.

The majority read "bi-zinati al-kawakib" with "zinat" in construct with "al-kawakib". The meaning: We adorned it with the beautifying of the stars, that is, with their beauty.

Masruq, al-A'mash, al-Nakha'i, and Hamzah read "zinatin" with tanwin and "al-kawakib" in the genitive, as a substitute (badal) for the adornment, the adornment being understood as a noun rather than a verbal noun. The construction after dropping the substituted-for noun is: We adorned the heaven with the stars, for the stars in themselves are a great adornment, since to the eyes of those who look at them they are like shining jewels.

'Asim, in the narration of Abu Bakr from him, read "zinatin" with tanwin and "al-kawakib" in the accusative, the adornment being a verbal noun whose agent is omitted; the meaning: that Allah adorned the stars by their being luminous and beautiful in themselves. Or the stars may be in the accusative by an implied "a'ni" (I mean), or as a substitute for "al-sama'" (the heaven) as a substitution of inclusion (badal ishtimal). The accusative of "hifzan" is as a verbal noun with an implied verb, meaning: We guarded it with a guarding; or as an object of purpose, meaning: We adorned it with the stars for protection; or by coordination with the position of "zinatin", as if He said: We created the stars as an adornment for the heaven.

﴿And as protection from every rebellious devil﴾: meaning, one who is defiant, outside obedience, who is pelted with the stars, as in His saying: ﴿And We have certainly adorned the nearest heaven with lamps and made them missiles against the devils﴾ [al-Mulk: 5].

The clause ﴿They cannot listen to the exalted assembly﴾ is a resumed sentence explaining their state after the heaven has been guarded against them.

Abu Hatim said: meaning, "so that they do not hear"; then he deleted "an" and so raised the verb. Al-Kalbi said likewise. The "exalted assembly" (al-mala' al-a'la) are the people of the nearest heaven and what is above it; all of them are called "exalted" by their being attributed to the assembly of the earth. The pronoun in "yassamma'una" refers to the devils.

It was said: the clause "la yassamma'una" is a description of "every devil". It was said: it is an answer to an implied question, as if it were said: "What was their state after the heaven was guarded against them?" and so He said: ﴿They cannot listen to the exalted assembly﴾. The majority read "yasma'una" with a sukun on the sin and lightening of the mim. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and 'Asim in the narration of Hafs from him read with doubling of the mim and the sin, the original being "yatasamma'una", with the ta' assimilated into the sin. The first reading indicates the negation of their hearing, without their listening; the second indicates the negation of both. In the sense of the first reading is His saying: ﴿Indeed, they are removed from hearing﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 212]. Mujahid said: "They used to eavesdrop, but they would not hear."

Abu 'Ubaydah preferred the second reading, saying: "Because the Arabs hardly say sami'tu ilayhi (I listened to him), but they say tasamma'tu ilayhi (I eavesdropped to him)."

﴿And they are pelted from every side, repelled﴾: meaning, they are struck from every side of the sky's sides with shooting stars when they try to ascend to steal hearing. The accusative of "duhuran" is as an object of purpose. Duhur means repelling; one says "dahartuhu dahran wa duhuran": I drove him away.

The majority read "duhuran" with a damma on the dal. 'Ali, al-Sulami, Ya'qub al-Hadrami, and Ibn Abi 'Ablah read it with a fatha.

It is narrated from Abu 'Amr that he read "yaqdhifun" in the active voice, but this reading does not conform to what is intended by the Qur'anic wording. It was said: the accusative of "duhuran" is as a circumstantial state (hal), meaning "madhurin" (repelled). It was said: it is the plural of "dahir", like "qa'id" and "qu'ud", and so it is also a state. It was said: it is a verbal noun of an implied verb, meaning "yudhharun duhuran" (they are repelled with repelling).

Al-Farra' said: the meaning is "they are pelted with what repels them", that is, with a repelling; then the preposition was deleted and the word became accusative by removal of the preposition.

It has been disputed whether this pelting of them with shooting stars occurred before the mission (al-mab'ath) or after it. Some said the former, others the latter. Another group said both are combined: the devils were not pelted before the mission with pelting that cut them off from hearing, but they were pelted at some times and not at others, and from one side and not from another. Then after the mission they were pelted at every time and from every side, until they were no longer able to steal any of the hearing except one who snatched a snatch, and a piercing flame followed him. The meaning of ﴿and for them is a perpetual punishment﴾ is: for them is a lasting punishment that does not cease, and what is meant is the punishment in the Hereafter, other than the punishment they receive in this world from the pelting with shooting stars.

Muqatil said: "that is, perpetual until the first blast." The first is preferable.

The majority of the exegetes held that al-wasib means the lasting. Al-Suddi, Abu Salih, and al-Kalbi said: it is the painful, whose pain reaches the heart, derived from al-wasab, which is sickness. It was said: it is the severe.

The exception in His saying ﴿except one who snatches a snatch﴾ is either from His saying ﴿they cannot listen﴾ or from His saying ﴿and they are pelted﴾.

It was said: the exception refers to other than revelation, given His saying ﴿Indeed, they are removed from hearing﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 212]; rather, one of them snatches a snatch of what the angels discuss among themselves and what will occur in the world before the people of the earth know it.

Al-Khatf is stealing by stealth and taking something quickly.

The majority read ﴿khatifa﴾ with a fatha on the kha' and a kasra on the ta', lightened. Qatadah and al-Hasan read with kasra on both and doubling of the ta'; this is the dialect of Tamim ibn Murr and Bakr ibn Wa'il. 'Isa ibn 'Umar read with a fatha on the kha' and a kasra on the ta' doubled. Ibn 'Abbas read with kasra on both and lightening of the ta'.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 37, verses 1–19 (part 2 of 2):

It has also been said that the exception (in ﴿except one who snatches a fragment﴾) is disjunctive (munqati'). ﴿Then a piercing flame pursued him﴾: that is, a piercing flame (shihab thaqib) overtook him and followed him. It is a shining star that burns him. Sometimes it does not burn him, and he throws what he snatched to his companions. The meteors with which the (devils) are pelted are not from the fixed stars but from other than the fixed stars. The root meaning of thuqub is brightness.

Al-Kisa'i said: "thaqabat al-nar yathqubu thaqabatan wa thuquban" means the fire blazed up. This verse is like His saying: ﴿except one who snatches a hearing, then a clear flame pursues him﴾ [al-Hijr: 18].

﴿So ask them: are they stronger in creation, or those whom We have created?﴾ That is: ask the disbelievers who deny the Resurrection whether they are stronger in creation, mightier in bodies and greater in limbs, or those whom We created, from the heavens and the earth and the angels? Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is: ask them a question of reproof (su'al taqrir): "Are they stronger in creation," that is, more perfect in workmanship, "or those whom We created before them from the earlier nations?" He means: they are not stronger in creation than the other nations, and We destroyed them for their denial, so what secures them from punishment? Then He mentioned the creation of man, saying: ﴿Indeed We created them from clay that adheres﴾. That is: indeed We created them, within the creation of their father Adam, from clay that adheres (lazib), that is, sticky. It is said: "lazaba yalzubu luzuban" means it clung. Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said: al-lazib is that which sticks. Ikrimah said: al-lazib is the sticky (lazij). Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: al-lazib is the good clay that clings to the hand. Mujahid said: it is al-lazim (the firm, constant), and the Arabs say: "tin lazib" and "tin lazim," substituting the "ba'" for the "mim." Al-lazim is that which is fixed, as it is said: "the matter became a lasting blow" (darbat lazib). From this is the saying of al-Nabighah:

Do not think good is without any evil after it,
nor think that evil is a lasting blow.

Al-Farra' related from the Arabs: "tin latib," meaning lazim, and al-latib is the fixed. Al-Asma'i said: al-latib is the adhering, like al-lazib.

The meaning of the verse is: how do these people find the Return far-fetched, when they were created from this weak creation, and yet one who was created with a creation stronger, greater, more complete and more perfect than theirs did not deny it? It has also been said: al-lazib is the foul-smelling (al-muntin), said by Mujahid and al-Dahhak.

Al-Jumhur (the majority of readers) read ﴿am man khalaqna﴾ with a shaddah on the mim, and it is the connective am (am al-muttasilah). Al-A'mash read it with a light (unshaddah) mim, and in his reading it is a second interrogative.

It has been said: "lazim" and "latib" have also been read (as variants), but I do not know who read that.

Then He (glorified is He) turned away from the previous speech and said: ﴿Rather, you (O Muhammad) are amazed﴾ at the power of Allah (glorified is He), ﴿and they mock﴾ you because of your amazement, or they mock you for what you say about affirming the Return.

Al-Jumhur read ﴿'ajibta﴾ with a fatha on the ta', in address to the Prophet (ﷺ). Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read it with a damma, and this reading was transmitted from Ali, Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas, and was chosen by Abu Ubayd and al-Farra'.

Al-Farra' said: the people read it with a fatha and a damma on the ta', and the damma is more beloved to me, because it is transmitted from Ali, Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) and Ibn Abbas.

He said: "The attribution of 'ajab (amazement) to Allah: its meaning from Allah is not like its meaning from the servants."

Al-Harawi said: some of the imams said: the meaning of His saying ﴿Rather, you are amazed﴾ is: rather, He recompensed them for their amazement, because Allah reported about them in more than one place their amazement at the creation, as He said: ﴿And they wondered that a warner from among them came to them﴾ [Sad: 4], and they said: ﴿Indeed this is a strange thing﴾ [Sad: 5], and ﴿Is it a marvel for the people that We revealed to a man from among them?﴾ [Yunus: 2].

Ali ibn Sulayman said: the meaning of the two readings is one, and the estimate is: "Say, O Muhammad, rather I am amazed," because the Prophet (ﷺ) is addressed by the Qur'an. Al-Nahhas said: this is a good view, and the omission of "say" (idmar al-qawl) is common.

It has also been said: the meaning of Allah's report about Himself with amazement is that there appeared from His command and His wrath upon those who disbelieved in Him something that stands in the place of amazement from creatures.

Al-Harawi said: it is said: the meaning of "'ajiba rabbukum" is: your Lord was pleased and rewarded, so He called it amazement, though it is not amazement in reality. So the meaning of "'ajibta" here is: their action was great in my sight. Al-Naqqash related that the meaning of "bal 'ajibta" is: rather, you denied (anka rta). Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: amazement from Allah is the denial of a thing and its magnification, and this is the language of the Arabs. It has also been said: its meaning is that He reached, in the completeness of His power and the abundance of His creatures, a point at which He was amazed by them, while these people, out of their ignorance, mock them. The waw in ﴿wa yaskhurun﴾ is for the state (hal), that is: rather you are amazed while they are mocking, and it may be for resumption (isti'naf).

﴿And when they are reminded, they do not remember﴾: that is, when they are admonished with an admonition from the admonitions of Allah or the admonitions of His Messenger, they do not remember, that is, they are not admonished by them and do not benefit from what is in them.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: that is, when they are told what befell the deniers among those before them, they turn away from it and do not reflect.

﴿And when they see a sign﴾: that is, a miracle from the miracles of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), ﴿they mock greatly﴾: that is, they exaggerate in mockery.

Qatadah said: they mock and say that it is mockery. It is said: "sakhira" and "istaskhara" have the same meaning, like "qarra" and "istaqarra," and "'ajiba" and "ista'jaba." The first (sakhira) is preferable, because the increase in the form indicates an increase in meaning.

It has also been said: the meaning of "yastaskhirun" is: they seek mockery from others. Mujahid said: they ridicule.

﴿And they say: this is nothing but manifest magic﴾: that is, what this is that you bring to us is nothing but clear, evident magic.

﴿When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be raised?﴾ The interrogative is for denial, that is: shall we be raised when we have died? The governing element of "idha" is what is indicated by ﴿shall we indeed be raised (a-innaa lamab'uthun)﴾, which is "a-nub'athu," since the one who is raised (mab'uthun) is not (the one who governs it), because of the intervention of what prevents its action in it. This denial of the Resurrection by them is the reason for which they denied the messengers and what was sent down to them, and mocked what they brought of miracles. The meaning of this verse has already been explained in several places.

﴿Or our forefathers, the earlier ones?﴾ It is a subject (mubtada') whose predicate is omitted, that is: "or our forefathers, the earlier ones, shall be raised?" It has been said: it is coordinated with the place (mahall) of "inna" and its noun. It has also been said: it is coordinated with the pronoun in "mab'uthun," because of the separation between them. The hamzah is for denial and enters upon the conjunction particle. For this reason al-Jumhur read it with a fatha on the waw, while Ibn 'Amir and Qalun read it with a sukun on it, on the basis that "aw" is the coordinating particle and the hamzah is not interrogative.

Then Allah (glorified is He) commanded His Messenger to answer on their behalf as a rebuke to them, saying: ﴿Say: yes, and you will be humbled﴾: that is, yes, you will be raised, and you will be abject and humiliated.

Al-Wahidi said: "al-dukhur" is the most severe of humiliation. The clause ﴿and you are humbled (wa antum dakhirun)﴾ is in the place of an accusative as a state (hal).

Then He (glorified is He) mentioned that their raising will occur with a single cry, saying: ﴿It will be but one shout﴾. The pronoun refers to the matter (al-qissah) or to the raising (al-ba'thah) understood from what precedes it, that is: the matter of the raising, or the raising, is but one shout, that is, one cry from Israfil by his blowing into the Trumpet at the Resurrection. ﴿Then behold, they will be looking﴾: that is, they will see what Allah does to them of punishment.

Al-Hasan said: it is the second blast. The cry was called "zajrah" because its purpose is rebuke (zajr). It has also been said: the meaning of "yanzurun" is "yantazirun," that is, they await what will be done to them. The first is preferable.

Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, and al-Hakim, who declared it sound, related through several chains from Ibn Mas'ud regarding ﴿By those who line up in rows﴾: he said: the angels. ﴿By those who drive with a driving﴾: he said: the angels. ﴿By those who recite a reminder﴾: he said: the angels.

Abd ibn Humayd related the same from Mujahid and Ikrimah. Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh in al-Azhamah related the same from Ibn Abbas.

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh related from him that he used to read ﴿they cannot listen to the exalted assembly﴾ with a light (mukhaffafah) sin, and said: they used to listen stealthily, but they could not listen.

Ibn Jarir related from him also, regarding His saying ﴿a perpetual punishment (adhab wasib)﴾: he said: lasting.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh in al-Azhamah related from him also: ﴿so a piercing flame pursued him﴾.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from him also regarding ﴿so a piercing flame pursued him﴾: he said: they are not killed by the flame and they do not die. But they are burned, injured and wounded, without being killed.

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him also regarding His saying ﴿from clay that adheres (min tin lazib)﴾: he said: sticking.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn al-Mundhir related from him also ﴿from clay that adheres﴾: he said: the sticky, good (clay).

Ibn Abi Hatim related from him also: he said: al-lazib, al-hama' (black mud) and al-tin are one: its beginning was dust, then it became foul-smelling black mud, then it became adhesive clay, and Allah created Adam from it.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Mas'ud: he said: al-lazib is that which sticks some of it to others.

Al-Firyabi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Hakim, who declared it sound, related from Ibn Mas'ud that he used to read ﴿Rather, you are amazed, and they mock﴾ with a damma on the ta' of "'ajibtu" (i.e., ﴿'ajibtu﴾, the speaker being Allah).

**Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 37, verses 20–49 (part 1 of 2)**

His words: ﴿They will say, "Woe to us!"﴾ That is, those who are resurrected will say, when they witness the Resurrection that they used to deny in the world: "Woe to us!" They call down woe upon themselves.

Al-Zajjaj said: "Al-waylu (woe) is a word that the speaker utters at the time of destruction." Al-Farra' said: "Its original form is *ya way lana*, and *way* means grief, as if he said: 'O grief for us!'"

Al-Nahhas said: "If it were as he said, it would have been written separately, but in the Mushaf it is written joined, and we know of no one who writes it except joined."

His words: ﴿This is the Day of Judgment﴾ is a justification for their calling woe upon themselves. *Al-din* means recompense. It is as if they said: "This is the day on which we will be recompensed for our deeds, of disbelief and denying the Messengers." The angels then answered them with their words: ﴿This is the Day of Decision, which you used to deny﴾. It is also permissible that this is the speech of some of them to others. *Al-fasl* means judgment and decree, because on that day a decision is made between the good-doer and the wrongdoer.

His words: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their spouses﴾ is a command from Allah, glorified is He, to the angels to gather the polytheists and their spouses, meaning those who resemble them in polytheism, who follow them in disbelief, and who support them in denying the Messengers. This is what Qatadah and Abu al-'Aliyah said.

Al-Hasan and Mujahid said: what is meant by "their spouses" is their polytheist wives who agreed with them in disbelief and wrongdoing.

Al-Dahhak said: "Their spouses are their companions from among the devils; every disbeliever is gathered with his devil." Muqatil also said this.

﴿And what they used to worship besides Allah﴾, from among the idols and the devils. This generality is derived from *ma* (the relative pronoun), since it refers to the things worshipped, not the worshippers. It is said to be restricted, because among the groups of disbelievers are those who worshipped the Messiah and those who worshipped the angels, and they are excluded by His words: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best (reward) has preceded from Us, they will be kept far from it﴾ [al-Anbiya': 101]. The reason for gathering the idols, even though they are inanimate and do not understand, is to increase the rebuke of their worshippers, to shame them, and to show that they neither benefit nor harm.

﴿So guide them to the path of Hellfire﴾, that is: make known to these gathered ones (p-1238) the way to the Fire and drive them toward it. It is said: *hadaytuhu al-tariq* and *hadaytuhu ilayha*, meaning I directed him to it. In this there is mockery of them.

﴿And stop them, for they are to be questioned﴾, that is: detain them. It is said: *waqaftu al-dabbah aqifuha waqfan*, and then *waqafat hiya wuqufan*, which is both transitive and intransitive. This detention occurs before they are driven to Hell, meaning: stop them for reckoning, then drive them to the Fire after that. The clause ﴿for they are to be questioned﴾ gives the reason for the first clause.

Al-Kalbi said: that is, they will be questioned about their deeds, their words, and their actions.

Al-Dahhak said: about their sins. It was also said: about "There is no god but Allah." It was also said: about wronging people. And it was also said: about wronging people.

It was said that this questioning is the one mentioned after this in His words: ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not help one another?﴾, that is: what is wrong with you that you do not help one another as you used to in the world? This is a rebuke, reproach, and mockery of them. Its original form is *tatanasarun*, and one of the two *ta'*s was dropped for lightness.

Al-Jumhur recited ﴿innahum mas'ulun﴾ with a kasrah on the hamzah. 'Isa ibn 'Umar recited it with a fathah.

Al-Kisa'i said: that is, "because they" or "that they." It was also said: the reference of His words ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not help one another?﴾ is to the words of Abu Jahl on the Day of Badr: ﴿We are a united company, victorious﴾ [al-Qamar: 44].

Then He, glorified is He, turned from what preceded to explain the state they are in at that moment, so He said: ﴿Rather, they are today in submission﴾, that is: surrendering, because they are unable to find a way out. Qatadah said: "submitting to the punishment of Allah." Al-Akhfash said: "casting down their hands." It is said: *istaslama lil-shay'* when one yields to something and humbles himself before it.

﴿And some of them turn to others, questioning one another﴾, that is: some of the disbelievers turn to others, questioning one another. It was said: they are the followers and the leaders, who question one another with questions of rebuke, reproach, and contention. Mujahid said: it is the saying of the disbelievers to the devils. Qatadah said: it is the saying of humans to the jinn. The first view is preferable because of His words: ﴿They will say, "Indeed you used to come to us from the right."﴾, that is: you used to come to us in the world from the right, meaning from the direction of truth, religion, and obedience, and you would turn us away from them.

Al-Zajjaj said: "You used to come to us from the direction of religion, and you made us see that religion and truth were what you misled us with. *Al-yamin* is an expression for truth." This is like His words, exalted is He, reporting about Iblis: ﴿Then I will surely come to them from before them, from behind them, from their right and from their left﴾ [al-A'raf: 17].

Al-Wahidi said: The people of the meanings (scholars) said: the leaders had sworn to these followers that what they called them to was the truth, so the followers trusted their oaths. So the meaning of ﴿you used to come to us from the right﴾ is: from the side of the oaths which you used to swear, so we trusted them. He said: "But the exegetes hold the first view."

It was also said: the meaning is: you used to come to us from the right that we love and take as a good omen, so that you would entice us by it, presenting it as sincere counsel. The Arabs take as a good omen what comes from the right and call it *al-sanih*.

It was also said: *al-yamin* means strength, that is: you used to restrain us by force, dominance, and coercion, as in His words: ﴿So he turned upon them, striking with the right hand﴾ [al-Saffat: 93], meaning with strength. This sentence is a new clause answering an implied question.

Likewise the clause ﴿They will say, "Rather, you were not believers"﴾ is a new clause answering an implied question. The meaning is: the leaders or devils said to these speakers, "You used to come to us from the right": "Rather, you were not believers, and we did not prevent you from faith."

The meaning is: you were never believers until we moved you from faith to disbelief. Rather, you were from the outset upon disbelief, and you persisted in it.

﴿And we had no authority over you﴾, that is: no dominance by coercion or force, so that we could bring you into faith or take you out of disbelief. ﴿Rather, you were a transgressing people﴾, that is: going beyond the limit in disbelief and misguidance.

His words: ﴿So the word of our Lord has come into effect upon us. Indeed, we are to taste (the punishment)﴾ are the words of the followed, meaning: the word of our Lord has become binding upon us and upon you, and has obligated us. They mean His words, exalted is He: ﴿I will surely fill Hell with you and whoever follows you among them, all together﴾ [Sad: 85]. (Indeed, we are tasters of the punishment), that is: all of us are tasters of the punishment that was promised. Al-Zajjaj said: "That is, the misleader and the misled are both in the Fire."

﴿So we misled you﴾, that is: we led you astray from guidance, invited you to what we were in of error, and made what you were upon of disbelief seem fair to you. ﴿Indeed, we were ourselves erring﴾. So there is no blame upon us for our targeting you for misguidance, because we wanted you to be like us in going astray. The meaning of the verse is: we proceeded to mislead you because we ourselves were described as being in error. Here they acknowledge that they caused their misguidance, but not through force or domination, and they deny what they said earlier, that they had coerced and overpowered them, so they said: ﴿And we had no authority over you﴾.

Then Allah, glorified is He, reported about the followers and the followed with His words: ﴿Indeed, they on that Day will be sharers in the punishment﴾, just as they were sharers in misguidance.

﴿Indeed, that is how We deal with the criminals﴾, that is: We deal in the same way with the criminals, that is, the people of crime, who are the polytheists.

As His words indicate: ﴿Indeed, they, when it was said to them, "There is no god but Allah," would become arrogant﴾, that is: when they were told, "Say: There is no god but Allah," they became arrogant and refused to accept it. The place of *yastakbirun* is in the accusative as the predicate of *kana*, or in the nominative as the predicate of *inna*, and *kana* here is *mulgha* (cancelled, i.e., with no governing effect).

﴿And they say, "Shall we really leave our gods for a mad poet?"﴾ They mean the Prophet (ﷺ), that is: for the words of a mad poet. Allah, glorified is He, responded to them with His words: ﴿Rather, he has brought the truth﴾, meaning the Qur'an, which includes monotheism, promise, and warning, ﴿and confirmed the Messengers﴾, that is: he confirmed them in what they brought of monotheism, warning, and the affirmation of the Last Abode, and did not oppose them, nor did he bring anything that the Messengers before him had not brought.

﴿Indeed, you will surely taste the painful punishment﴾, that is: indeed, because of your polytheism and your denial, you will surely taste the severely painful punishment.

Al-Jumhur recited ﴿la-dha'iqu﴾ with the *nun* dropped and *al-'adhab* in the genitive.
