The exception is either connected, on the assumption that the address in *tujzawna* ("you are recompensed") is general to all the responsible, or disconnected, meaning: but the chosen servants of Allah will not taste the punishment.

The reference of His words ﴿those﴾ is to the sincere ones, and it is the subject (*mubtada'*), whose predicate is His words: ﴿For them is a known provision﴾, that is: for these sincere ones is a provision which Allah provides for them, known in its goodness, its pleasantness, and its being unending.

Qatadah said: "That refers to Paradise." It was also said: "It is known in its time, namely that they will be given it morning and evening, as in His words: ﴿And for them is their provision therein, morning and evening﴾ [Maryam: 62]." It was also said: it is what is mentioned in His words after it.

﴿Fruits﴾: this is either a substitute (*badal*) for *rizq* (provision), or the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: it is fruits. This is the apparent meaning.

*Al-fawakih* is the plural of *al-fakihah*, which means all fruits, both fresh and dry. Fruits are singled out for mention because all the provisions of the people of Paradise are fruits, so it is said. But the better view is that they are singled out because they are the most delicious of what they eat and the most pleasing to their souls. It was also said: fruits are the accompaniment of all other foods, so mentioning them makes mention of others unnecessary.

His words: ﴿And they will be honored﴾ are in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (*hal*), meaning: they will receive from Allah, mighty and majestic is He, a great honor, by raising their ranks with Him, hearing His speech, and meeting Him in Paradise. Al-Jumhur recited *mukramun* with the *ra'* lightened. Abu Miqsam recited it with the *ra'* doubled.

His words: ﴿in the Gardens of Bliss﴾ may be connected to *mukramun*, or be a second predicate, or be a circumstantial clause.

His words: ﴿upon thrones﴾ may be a circumstantial clause, or a third predicate. The accusative of ﴿facing one another﴾ is a circumstantial clause from the pronoun in *mukramun*, or from the pronoun in the complement of "upon thrones."

Ikrimah and Mujahid said: the meaning of facing one another is that none of them looks at the back of another. It was also said: the thrones turn them around however they wish, so none of them sees the back of another.

Al-Jumhur recited *surur* (thrones) with a *damma* on the *ra'*. Abu al-Simak recited it with a fathah, which is the dialect of some of the Tamim tribe.

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned another attribute of theirs, saying: ﴿A cup from a flowing spring will be passed around to them﴾. This sentence may be a new clause answering an implied question, or it may be in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause from the pronoun in *mutaqabilin*. The *ka's* (cup), according to the lexicographers, is a term for any vessel containing drink, so if it is empty, it is not a *ka's*.

Al-Dahhak and al-Sudi said: every *ka's* in the Qur'an is wine.

Al-Nahhas said: "Some reliable lexicographers have reported that the Arabs call a goblet a *ka's* when it contains wine, but when it contains no wine it is a *qadah* (bowl), just as a tray is called *ma'ida* when it has food on it, and if it has no food on it, it is not called *ma'ida*." And ﴿from a flowing spring﴾ is connected to an omitted word which is an attribute of *ka's*.

**Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 37, verses 20–49 (part 2 of 2):**

Al-Zajjaj said: ﴿with a cup from a flowing spring﴾ means: from wine that flows as springs flow over the surface of the earth. *Ma'in* is flowing water.

His saying ﴿white, delicious to the drinkers﴾ are two attributes of *ka's* (cup).

Al-Zajjaj said: that is, *dhat ladhdha* (possessing deliciousness), so the noun modified was omitted. It is also permissible for the attribute to be the verbal noun *ladhdha* (delight) for the sake of emphasis on its being pure delight, so there is no need to posit an omitted noun.

Al-Hasan said: The wine of Paradise is whiter than milk and has a delicious taste. It is said: *sharab ladhdh* and *sharab ladhidh* (a delightful drink), just as it is said: *nabat ghadd* and *ghadid* (tender plant). From this is the saying of the poet:

*"With her sweet speech, which, if she spoke to the lions of the desert with it, they would come swiftly."*

*Al-ladhidh* is everything that is found pleasant. It was also said: *al-bayda'* is the one that men have not pressed.

Then He described this cup of wine by what differs from the wine of this world, saying: ﴿No ghawl is in it﴾, meaning: it does not seize their minds so as to carry them away, and no illness or headache afflicts them from it. ﴿Nor are they intoxicated by it﴾, meaning: they do not become drunk. It is said: *nazafa al-sharib* so he is *manzuf* and *nazif* when he becomes drunk. From this is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

*"And when she walks, like the walk of the nazif, she is overcome by the breathlessness among the sand dunes."*

He also said:

*"A nazif, when she stands for a face, sways."*

From this is the saying of another:

*"So I kissed her mouth, seizing her horns, drinking like the nazif with the cold water of al-Hashraj."*

Al-Farra' said: The Arabs say *laysa fiha ghilah wa ghā'ila wa ghawl* (there is no ghilah, ghā'ila, or ghawl in it), all meaning the same.

Abu Ubayda said: *al-ghawl* is that it seizes their minds. He cited the verse of Mut'i' ibn Iyas:

*"The cup did not cease to seize them, and to take away the first and the foremost."*

Al-Wahidi said: The essential meaning of *al-ghawl* is destruction. It is said: *ghālahu ghawlan* and *ightālahu*, meaning he destroyed him. *Al-ghawl* is everything that seizes you, i.e., destroys you.

The majority of readers recited ﴿yunzafun﴾ with a *dammah* on the *ya'* and a *fatha* on the *za'*, in the passive voice.

Hamza and al-Kisa'i recited it with a *dammah* on the *ya'* and a *kasra* on the *za'*, from *anzafa al-rajul*, when his mind departed due to drunkenness, so he is *nazif*, *manzuf*, and *munzif*. It is said: *ahsud al-zar'* when its harvest has come, and *aqtif al-karm* when its gathering has come.

Al-Farra' said: Whoever recites with a *kasra* on the *za'* has two meanings: it is said *anzafa al-rajul* when his wine has run out, and *anzafa* when his mind has departed due to drunkenness. This reading may be understood to mean that their drink does not run out, for the sake of added benefit.

Al-Nahhas said: The first reading is clearer and more correct in meaning, because the meaning of ﴿la yunzafun﴾ according to the majority of the exegetes is: their minds do not depart. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, negated from the wine of Paradise the afflictions that befall the wine of this world, from headache and intoxication.

Al-Zajjaj and Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said that the meaning of *la yanzifun* with a *kasra* on the *za'* is: they do not become drunk.

Al-Mahdawi said: The meaning of *yunzafun* cannot be "they become drunk," because before it is ﴿no ghawl is in it﴾, i.e., it does not seize their minds, so it would be a repetition. This supports what Qatada said: that *al-ghawl* is stomach ache, and so Ibn Abi Najih narrated from Mujahid. Al-Hasan said: *al-ghawl* is headache. Ibn Kaysan said: it is colic. So the meaning of the verse is: there is in it no kind of corruption that accompanies the drinking of wine in this world, whether colic, stomach ache, headache, rowdiness, idle talk, or sinfulness, and they are not drunk from it.

This is supported by the fact that the origin of *al-ghawl* is corruption that strikes in secret. It is said: *ightālahu ightiyālan* when he corrupted his affair in secret. From this comes *al-ghawl* and *al-ghīla*, killing in secret.

Ibn Abi Ishaq recited ﴿yunzifun﴾ with a *fatha* on the *ya'* and a *kasra* on the *za'*.

Talha ibn Musarrif recited it with a *fatha* on the *ya'* and a *dammah* on the *za'*.

When He, glorified be He, mentioned the description of their drink, He mentioned right after it the description of their spouses, saying: ﴿And with them are those restraining their gaze﴾, meaning: women who restrain their gaze to their husbands, so they do not desire others. *Al-qasr* means confinement, and from this is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

*"Of the women restraining the gaze, if a tiny ant crawled upon her shirt, it would leave a mark."*

*Al-muhwil* is the small ant, and *al-itb* is the shirt. It was said: *al-qasirat* are those confined to their husbands. The first is preferable, because He said *qasirat al-tarf* and did not say *maqsurat*.

*Al-'in* is the plural of *'ayna'*, which is the woman with large eyes.

Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of *'in* is large eyes and beautiful ones. Mujahid said: *al-'in* are those with beautiful eyes.

Al-Hasan said: They are those who have intense whiteness of the eye and intense blackness of it, and the first is preferable.

﴿As if they were hidden eggs﴾. Al-Hasan and Abu Zayd said: He likened them to ostrich eggs which the ostrich covers with feathers from the wind and dust, so their color is white tinged with yellow, which is the most beautiful of women's colors.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi said: He likened them to the inner part of the egg before it is peeled and touched by hands, and Ibn Jarir also said this. From this is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

*"And an egg of a curtained tent, whose tent is not approached, I enjoyed from play with her without haste."*

Al-Mubarrad said: The Arabs say, when they describe a thing with beauty and cleanliness, "as if it were ostrich eggs covered with feathers."

It was also said: *al-maknun* is the one protected from breaking, meaning they are virgins. It was also said: the intended *al-bayd* is pearls, as in His saying: ﴿And wide-eyed maidens, like hidden pearls﴾ [al-Waqi'a: 22–23]. Similar to this is the saying of the poet:

*"And she is white like a pearl of al-Ghawwas, distinguished from a hidden jewel."*

The first is preferable. He said *maknun* and did not say *maknunat*, because He described the eggs in respect of the wording.

Ibn Abi Hatim recorded from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their spouses﴾, that he said: The angels say this saying to the guards of Hell.

Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Ibn Abi Shayba, Ibn Mani' in his Musnad, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th recorded through the route of al-Nu'man ibn Bashir from Umar ibn al-Khattab regarding His saying: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their spouses﴾, that he said: their likes, those who are like them: the people of usury come with the people of usury, the people of fornication with the people of fornication, and the people of wine with the people of wine, spouses in Paradise and spouses in the Fire.

Al-Firyabi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shayba, Ibn al-Mundhir, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th recorded from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their spouses﴾, that he said: their likes, and in another wording: their counterparts.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim recorded from him regarding His saying: ﴿So guide them to the path of Hellfire﴾, that he said: direct them. Ibn Abi Hatim also recorded from him in the verse, he said: guide them ﴿to the path of Hellfire﴾, he said: the path of the Fire.

He also recorded from him regarding His saying: ﴿And stop them, indeed they are to be questioned﴾, that he said: hold them, indeed they are to be called to account.

Al-Bukhari in his History, al-Darimi, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), and Ibn Mardawayh recorded from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is no caller who calls to something except that he will be made to stand with it on the Day of Resurrection, bound to it, never separating from it, even if a man calls a man." Then he recited: ﴿And stop them, indeed they are to be questioned﴾.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim recorded from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And some of them will turn to others, questioning one another﴾, that he said: that is when they are raised at the second blast.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh recorded from him regarding His saying: ﴿When it was said to them, "There is no god but Allah," they became arrogant﴾, that he said: they were disdainful when no partner was associated with Allah. ﴿And they say, "Shall we really leave our gods for a mad poet?"﴾, which is not sensible. He said: Allah related his truthfulness, so He said: ﴿Rather, he has brought the truth and confirmed the messengers﴾.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat recorded from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have been commanded to fight the people until they say 'There is no god but Allah.' Whoever says 'There is no god but Allah' has protected his property and his life from me, except by its right, and his account is with Allah."

Allah revealed in His Book, mentioning a people who were arrogant, saying: ﴿Indeed, they, when it was said to them, "There is no god but Allah," were arrogant﴾, and He said: ﴿When those who disbelieved put into their hearts zealotry, the zealotry of ignorance, then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers and made them adhere to the word of righteousness, and they were more deserving of it and worthy of it﴾ [al-Fath: 26]. It is the statement "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." The polytheists were arrogant toward it on the day of al-Hudaybiyya, the day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made the treaty with them for the term of truce.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th recorded from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿A cup from a flowing spring is passed around among them﴾, that he said: it is wine. ﴿No ghawl is in it﴾, he said: there is no headache in it. ﴿Nor are they intoxicated by it﴾, he said: their minds do not depart.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh recorded from him that he said regarding wine: it has four properties: intoxication, headache, vomiting, and urination. So Allah cleansed the wine of Paradise of them, saying: ﴿No ghawl is in it﴾, its minds are not seized by intoxication, ﴿nor are they intoxicated by it﴾, he said: they vomit from it as the owner of the wine of this world vomits from it.

Ibn Jarir recorded from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿No ghawl is in it﴾, he said: it is wine, there is no stomach ache in it.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th also recorded from him regarding His saying: ﴿And with them are those restraining their gaze﴾, he said: from other than their husbands. ﴿As if they were hidden eggs﴾, he said: hidden pearls.

Ibn al-Mundhir recorded from him regarding His saying: ﴿As if they were hidden eggs﴾, he said: the whiteness of the egg, from which its membrane and covering have been removed.

**Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 37, verses 20–49 (part 1 of 2)**

His words: ﴿They will say, "Woe to us!"﴾ That is, those who are resurrected will say, when they witness the Resurrection that they used to deny in the world: "Woe to us!" They call down woe upon themselves.

Al-Zajjaj said: "Al-waylu (woe) is a word that the speaker utters at the time of destruction." Al-Farra' said: "Its original form is *ya way lana*, and *way* means grief, as if he said: 'O grief for us!'"

Al-Nahhas said: "If it were as he said, it would have been written separately, but in the Mushaf it is written joined, and we know of no one who writes it except joined."

His words: ﴿This is the Day of Judgment﴾ is a justification for their calling woe upon themselves. *Al-din* means recompense. It is as if they said: "This is the day on which we will be recompensed for our deeds, of disbelief and denying the Messengers." The angels then answered them with their words: ﴿This is the Day of Decision, which you used to deny﴾. It is also permissible that this is the speech of some of them to others. *Al-fasl* means judgment and decree, because on that day a decision is made between the good-doer and the wrongdoer.

His words: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their spouses﴾ is a command from Allah, glorified is He, to the angels to gather the polytheists and their spouses, meaning those who resemble them in polytheism, who follow them in disbelief, and who support them in denying the Messengers. This is what Qatadah and Abu al-'Aliyah said.

Al-Hasan and Mujahid said: what is meant by "their spouses" is their polytheist wives who agreed with them in disbelief and wrongdoing.

Al-Dahhak said: "Their spouses are their companions from among the devils; every disbeliever is gathered with his devil." Muqatil also said this.

﴿And what they used to worship besides Allah﴾, from among the idols and the devils. This generality is derived from *ma* (the relative pronoun), since it refers to the things worshipped, not the worshippers. It is said to be restricted, because among the groups of disbelievers are those who worshipped the Messiah and those who worshipped the angels, and they are excluded by His words: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best (reward) has preceded from Us, they will be kept far from it﴾ [al-Anbiya': 101]. The reason for gathering the idols, even though they are inanimate and do not understand, is to increase the rebuke of their worshippers, to shame them, and to show that they neither benefit nor harm.

﴿So guide them to the path of Hellfire﴾, that is: make known to these gathered ones (p-1238) the way to the Fire and drive them toward it. It is said: *hadaytuhu al-tariq* and *hadaytuhu ilayha*, meaning I directed him to it. In this there is mockery of them.

﴿And stop them, for they are to be questioned﴾, that is: detain them. It is said: *waqaftu al-dabbah aqifuha waqfan*, and then *waqafat hiya wuqufan*, which is both transitive and intransitive. This detention occurs before they are driven to Hell, meaning: stop them for reckoning, then drive them to the Fire after that. The clause ﴿for they are to be questioned﴾ gives the reason for the first clause.

Al-Kalbi said: that is, they will be questioned about their deeds, their words, and their actions.

Al-Dahhak said: about their sins. It was also said: about "There is no god but Allah." It was also said: about wronging people. And it was also said: about wronging people.

It was said that this questioning is the one mentioned after this in His words: ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not help one another?﴾, that is: what is wrong with you that you do not help one another as you used to in the world? This is a rebuke, reproach, and mockery of them. Its original form is *tatanasarun*, and one of the two *ta'*s was dropped for lightness.

Al-Jumhur recited ﴿innahum mas'ulun﴾ with a kasrah on the hamzah. 'Isa ibn 'Umar recited it with a fathah.

Al-Kisa'i said: that is, "because they" or "that they." It was also said: the reference of His words ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not help one another?﴾ is to the words of Abu Jahl on the Day of Badr: ﴿We are a united company, victorious﴾ [al-Qamar: 44].

Then He, glorified is He, turned from what preceded to explain the state they are in at that moment, so He said: ﴿Rather, they are today in submission﴾, that is: surrendering, because they are unable to find a way out. Qatadah said: "submitting to the punishment of Allah." Al-Akhfash said: "casting down their hands." It is said: *istaslama lil-shay'* when one yields to something and humbles himself before it.

﴿And some of them turn to others, questioning one another﴾, that is: some of the disbelievers turn to others, questioning one another. It was said: they are the followers and the leaders, who question one another with questions of rebuke, reproach, and contention. Mujahid said: it is the saying of the disbelievers to the devils. Qatadah said: it is the saying of humans to the jinn. The first view is preferable because of His words: ﴿They will say, "Indeed you used to come to us from the right."﴾, that is: you used to come to us in the world from the right, meaning from the direction of truth, religion, and obedience, and you would turn us away from them.

Al-Zajjaj said: "You used to come to us from the direction of religion, and you made us see that religion and truth were what you misled us with. *Al-yamin* is an expression for truth." This is like His words, exalted is He, reporting about Iblis: ﴿Then I will surely come to them from before them, from behind them, from their right and from their left﴾ [al-A'raf: 17].

Al-Wahidi said: The people of the meanings (scholars) said: the leaders had sworn to these followers that what they called them to was the truth, so the followers trusted their oaths. So the meaning of ﴿you used to come to us from the right﴾ is: from the side of the oaths which you used to swear, so we trusted them. He said: "But the exegetes hold the first view."

It was also said: the meaning is: you used to come to us from the right that we love and take as a good omen, so that you would entice us by it, presenting it as sincere counsel. The Arabs take as a good omen what comes from the right and call it *al-sanih*.

It was also said: *al-yamin* means strength, that is: you used to restrain us by force, dominance, and coercion, as in His words: ﴿So he turned upon them, striking with the right hand﴾ [al-Saffat: 93], meaning with strength. This sentence is a new clause answering an implied question.

Likewise the clause ﴿They will say, "Rather, you were not believers"﴾ is a new clause answering an implied question. The meaning is: the leaders or devils said to these speakers, "You used to come to us from the right": "Rather, you were not believers, and we did not prevent you from faith."

The meaning is: you were never believers until we moved you from faith to disbelief. Rather, you were from the outset upon disbelief, and you persisted in it.

﴿And we had no authority over you﴾, that is: no dominance by coercion or force, so that we could bring you into faith or take you out of disbelief. ﴿Rather, you were a transgressing people﴾, that is: going beyond the limit in disbelief and misguidance.

His words: ﴿So the word of our Lord has come into effect upon us. Indeed, we are to taste (the punishment)﴾ are the words of the followed, meaning: the word of our Lord has become binding upon us and upon you, and has obligated us. They mean His words, exalted is He: ﴿I will surely fill Hell with you and whoever follows you among them, all together﴾ [Sad: 85]. (Indeed, we are tasters of the punishment), that is: all of us are tasters of the punishment that was promised. Al-Zajjaj said: "That is, the misleader and the misled are both in the Fire."

﴿So we misled you﴾, that is: we led you astray from guidance, invited you to what we were in of error, and made what you were upon of disbelief seem fair to you. ﴿Indeed, we were ourselves erring﴾. So there is no blame upon us for our targeting you for misguidance, because we wanted you to be like us in going astray. The meaning of the verse is: we proceeded to mislead you because we ourselves were described as being in error. Here they acknowledge that they caused their misguidance, but not through force or domination, and they deny what they said earlier, that they had coerced and overpowered them, so they said: ﴿And we had no authority over you﴾.

Then Allah, glorified is He, reported about the followers and the followed with His words: ﴿Indeed, they on that Day will be sharers in the punishment﴾, just as they were sharers in misguidance.

﴿Indeed, that is how We deal with the criminals﴾, that is: We deal in the same way with the criminals, that is, the people of crime, who are the polytheists.

As His words indicate: ﴿Indeed, they, when it was said to them, "There is no god but Allah," would become arrogant﴾, that is: when they were told, "Say: There is no god but Allah," they became arrogant and refused to accept it. The place of *yastakbirun* is in the accusative as the predicate of *kana*, or in the nominative as the predicate of *inna*, and *kana* here is *mulgha* (cancelled, i.e., with no governing effect).

﴿And they say, "Shall we really leave our gods for a mad poet?"﴾ They mean the Prophet (ﷺ), that is: for the words of a mad poet. Allah, glorified is He, responded to them with His words: ﴿Rather, he has brought the truth﴾, meaning the Qur'an, which includes monotheism, promise, and warning, ﴿and confirmed the Messengers﴾, that is: he confirmed them in what they brought of monotheism, warning, and the affirmation of the Last Abode, and did not oppose them, nor did he bring anything that the Messengers before him had not brought.

﴿Indeed, you will surely taste the painful punishment﴾, that is: indeed, because of your polytheism and your denial, you will surely taste the severely painful punishment.

Al-Jumhur recited ﴿la-dha'iqu﴾ with the *nun* dropped and *al-'adhab* in the genitive. Aban ibn Tha'lab, on the authority of 'Asim, and Abu al-Simak recited it with the *nun* dropped and *al-'adhab* in the accusative. Sibawayh cited, as an example of this recitation with the dropped *nun* and the accusative for *al-'adhab*, the verse of the poet:

*So I found him not seeking to appease, nor remembering God except a little.*

Sibawayh also permitted *wal-muqimi al-salah* (al-Hajj: 35) with *al-salah* in the accusative on this analysis. It has also been recited with the *nun* retained and *al-'adhab* in the accusative, in accordance with the original form.

Then He, glorified is He, explained that what they tasted of punishment was only because of their deeds, so He said: ﴿And you are not recompensed except for what you used to do﴾, that is: you are recompensed only for what you used to do of disbelief and sins, or: only because of what you used to do.

Then He excepted the believers, saying: ﴿Except the chosen servants of Allah﴾. The people of Madinah and Kufah recited *al-mukhlasin* (p-1239) with a fathah on the *lam*, meaning: those whom Allah chose for His obedience and monotheism.

The rest recited it with a kasrah, meaning: those who made their worship and monotheism sincerely for Allah. The exception is either connected, on the assumption that the address in *tujzawna* ("you are recompensed") is general to all the responsible, or disconnected, meaning: but the chosen servants of Allah will not taste the punishment.

The reference of His words ﴿those﴾ is to the sincere ones, and it is the subject (*mubtada'*), whose predicate is His words: ﴿For them is a known provision﴾, that is: for these sincere ones is a provision which Allah provides for them, known in its goodness, its pleasantness, and its being unending.

Qatadah said: "That refers to Paradise." It was also said: "It is known in its time, namely that they will be given it morning and evening, as in His words: ﴿And for them is their provision therein, morning and evening﴾ [Maryam: 62]." It was also said: it is what is mentioned in His words after it.

﴿Fruits﴾: this is either a substitute (*badal*) for *rizq* (provision), or the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: it is fruits. This is the apparent meaning.

*Al-fawakih* is the plural of *al-fakihah*, which means all fruits, both fresh and dry. Fruits are singled out for mention because all the provisions of the people of Paradise are fruits, so it is said. But the better view is that they are singled out because they are the most delicious of what they eat and the most pleasing to their souls. It was also said: fruits are the accompaniment of all other foods, so mentioning them makes mention of others unnecessary.

His words: ﴿And they will be honored﴾ are in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (*hal*), meaning: they will receive from Allah, mighty and majestic is He, a great honor, by raising their ranks with Him, hearing His speech, and meeting Him in Paradise. Al-Jumhur recited *mukramun* with the *ra'* lightened. Abu Miqsam recited it with the *ra'* doubled.

His words: ﴿in the Gardens of Bliss﴾ may be connected to *mukramun*, or be a second predicate, or be a circumstantial clause.

His words: ﴿upon thrones﴾ may be a circumstantial clause, or a third predicate. The accusative of ﴿facing one another﴾ is a circumstantial clause from the pronoun in *mukramun*, or from the pronoun in the complement of "upon thrones."

Ikrimah and Mujahid said: the meaning of facing one another is that none of them looks at the back of another. It was also said: the thrones turn them around however they wish, so none of them sees the back of another.

Al-Jumhur recited *surur* (thrones) with a *damma* on the *ra'*. Abu al-Simak recited it with a fathah, which is the dialect of some of the Tamim tribe.

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned another attribute of theirs, saying: ﴿A cup from a flowing spring will be passed around to them﴾. This sentence may be a new clause answering an implied question, or it may be in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause from the pronoun in *mutaqabilin*. The *ka's* (cup), according to the lexicographers, is a term for any vessel containing drink, so if it is empty, it is not a *ka's*.

Al-Dahhak and al-Sudi said: every *ka's* in the Qur'an is wine.

Al-Nahhas said: "Some reliable lexicographers have reported that the Arabs call a goblet a *ka's* when it contains wine, but when it contains no wine it is a *qadah* (bowl), just as a tray is called *ma'ida* when it has food on it, and if it has no food on it, it is not called *ma'ida*." And ﴿from a flowing spring﴾ is connected to an omitted word which is an attribute of *ka's*.

**Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 37, verses 20–49 (part 2 of 2):**

Al-Zajjaj said: ﴿with a cup from a flowing spring﴾ means: from wine that flows as springs flow over the surface of the earth. *Ma'in* is flowing water.

His saying ﴿white, delicious to the drinkers﴾ are two attributes of *ka's* (cup).

Al-Zajjaj said: that is, *dhat ladhdha* (possessing deliciousness), so the noun modified was omitted. It is also permissible for the attribute to be the verbal noun *ladhdha* (delight) for the sake of emphasis on its being pure delight, so there is no need to posit an omitted noun.

Al-Hasan said: The wine of Paradise is whiter than milk and has a delicious taste. It is said: *sharab ladhdh* and *sharab ladhidh* (a delightful drink), just as it is said: *nabat ghadd* and *ghadid* (tender plant). From this is the saying of the poet:

*"With her sweet speech, which, if she spoke to the lions of the desert with it, they would come swiftly."*

*Al-ladhidh* is everything that is found pleasant. It was also said: *al-bayda'* is the one that men have not pressed.

Then He described this cup of wine by what differs from the wine of this world, saying: ﴿No ghawl is in it﴾, meaning: it does not seize their minds so as to carry them away, and no illness or headache afflicts them from it. ﴿Nor are they intoxicated by it﴾, meaning: they do not become drunk. It is said: *nazafa al-sharib* so he is *manzuf* and *nazif* when he becomes drunk. From this is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

*"And when she walks, like the walk of the nazif, she is overcome by the breathlessness among the sand dunes."*

He also said:

*"A nazif, when she stands for a face, sways."*

From this is the saying of another:

*"So I kissed her mouth, seizing her horns, drinking like the nazif with the cold water of al-Hashraj."*

Al-Farra' said: The Arabs say *laysa fiha ghilah wa ghā'ila wa ghawl* (there is no ghilah, ghā'ila, or ghawl in it), all meaning the same.

Abu Ubayda said: *al-ghawl* is that it seizes their minds. He cited the verse of Mut'i' ibn Iyas:

*"The cup did not cease to seize them, and to take away the first and the foremost."*

Al-Wahidi said: The essential meaning of *al-ghawl* is destruction. It is said: *ghālahu ghawlan* and *ightālahu*, meaning he destroyed him. *Al-ghawl* is everything that seizes you, i.e., destroys you.

The majority of readers recited ﴿yunzafun﴾ with a *dammah* on the *ya'* and a *fatha* on the *za'*, in the passive voice.

Hamza and al-Kisa'i recited it with a *dammah* on the *ya'* and a *kasra* on the *za'*, from *anzafa al-rajul*, when his mind departed due to drunkenness, so he is *nazif*, *manzuf*, and *munzif*. It is said: *ahsud al-zar'* when its harvest has come, and *aqtif al-karm* when its gathering has come.

Al-Farra' said: Whoever recites with a *kasra* on the *za'* has two meanings: it is said *anzafa al-rajul* when his wine has run out, and *anzafa* when his mind has departed due to drunkenness. This reading may be understood to mean that their drink does not run out, for the sake of added benefit.

Al-Nahhas said: The first reading is clearer and more correct in meaning, because the meaning of ﴿la yunzafun﴾ according to the majority of the exegetes is: their minds do not depart. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, negated from the wine of Paradise the afflictions that befall the wine of this world, from headache and intoxication.

Al-Zajjaj and Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said that the meaning of *la yanzifun* with a *kasra* on the *za'* is: they do not become drunk.

Al-Mahdawi said: The meaning of *yunzafun* cannot be "they become drunk," because before it is ﴿no ghawl is in it﴾, i.e., it does not seize their minds, so it would be a repetition. This supports what Qatada said: that *al-ghawl* is stomach ache, and so Ibn Abi Najih narrated from Mujahid. Al-Hasan said: *al-ghawl* is headache. Ibn Kaysan said: it is colic. So the meaning of the verse is: there is in it no kind of corruption that accompanies the drinking of wine in this world, whether colic, stomach ache, headache, rowdiness, idle talk, or sinfulness, and they are not drunk from it.

This is supported by the fact that the origin of *al-ghawl* is corruption that strikes in secret. It is said: *ightālahu ightiyālan* when he corrupted his affair in secret. From this comes *al-ghawl* and *al-ghīla*, killing in secret.

Ibn Abi Ishaq recited ﴿yunzifun﴾ with a *fatha* on the *ya'* and a *kasra* on the *za'*.

Talha ibn Musarrif recited it with a *fatha* on the *ya'* and a *dammah* on the *za'*.

When He, glorified be He, mentioned the description of their drink, He mentioned right after it the description of their spouses, saying: ﴿And with them are those restraining their gaze﴾, meaning: women who restrain their gaze to their husbands, so they do not desire others. *Al-qasr* means confinement, and from this is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

*"Of the women restraining the gaze, if a tiny ant crawled upon her shirt, it would leave a mark."*

*Al-muhwil* is the small ant, and *al-itb* is the shirt. It was said: *al-qasirat* are those confined to their husbands. The first is preferable, because He said *qasirat al-tarf* and did not say *maqsurat*.

*Al-'in* is the plural of *'ayna'*, which is the woman with large eyes.

Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of *'in* is large eyes and beautiful ones. Mujahid said: *al-'in* are those with beautiful eyes.

Al-Hasan said: They are those who have intense whiteness of the eye and intense blackness of it, and the first is preferable.

﴿As if they were hidden eggs﴾. Al-Hasan and Abu Zayd said: He likened them to ostrich eggs which the ostrich covers with feathers from the wind and dust, so their color is white tinged with yellow, which is the most beautiful of women's colors.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi said: He likened them to the inner part of the egg before it is peeled and touched by hands, and Ibn Jarir also said this. From this is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

*"And an egg of a curtained tent, whose tent is not approached, I enjoyed from play with her without haste."*

Al-Mubarrad said: The Arabs say, when they describe a thing with beauty and cleanliness, "as if it were ostrich eggs covered with feathers."

It was also said: *al-maknun* is the one protected from breaking, meaning they are virgins. It was also said: the intended *al-bayd* is pearls, as in His saying: ﴿And wide-eyed maidens, like hidden pearls﴾ [al-Waqi'a: 22–23]. Similar to this is the saying of the poet:

*"And she is white like a pearl of al-Ghawwas, distinguished from a hidden jewel."*

The first is preferable. He said *maknun* and did not say *maknunat*, because He described the eggs in respect of the wording.

Ibn Abi Hatim recorded from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their spouses﴾, that he said: The angels say this saying to the guards of Hell.

Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Ibn Abi Shayba, Ibn Mani' in his Musnad, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th recorded through the route of al-Nu'man ibn Bashir from Umar ibn al-Khattab regarding His saying: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their spouses﴾, that he said: their likes, those who are like them: the people of usury come with the people of usury, the people of fornication with the people of fornication, and the people of wine with the people of wine, spouses in Paradise and spouses in the Fire.

Al-Firyabi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shayba, Ibn al-Mundhir, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th recorded from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their spouses﴾, that he said: their likes, and in another wording: their counterparts.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim recorded from him regarding His saying: ﴿So guide them to the path of Hellfire﴾, that he said: direct them. Ibn Abi Hatim also recorded from him in the verse, he said: guide them ﴿to the path of Hellfire﴾, he said: the path of the Fire.

He also recorded from him regarding His saying: ﴿And stop them, indeed they are to be questioned﴾, that he said: hold them, indeed they are to be called to account.

Al-Bukhari in his History, al-Darimi, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), and Ibn Mardawayh recorded from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is no caller who calls to something except that he will be made to stand with it on the Day of Resurrection, bound to it, never separating from it, even if a man calls a man." Then he recited: ﴿And stop them, indeed they are to be questioned﴾.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim recorded from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And some of them will turn to others, questioning one another﴾, that he said: that is when they are raised at the second blast.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh recorded from him regarding His saying: ﴿When it was said to them, "There is no god but Allah," they became arrogant﴾, that he said: they were disdainful when no partner was associated with Allah. ﴿And they say, "Shall we really leave our gods for a mad poet?"﴾, which is not sensible. He said: Allah related his truthfulness, so He said: ﴿Rather, he has brought the truth and confirmed the messengers﴾.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat recorded from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have been commanded to fight the people until they say 'There is no god but Allah.' Whoever says 'There is no god but Allah' has protected his property and his life from me, except by its right, and his account is with Allah."

Allah revealed in His Book, mentioning a people who were arrogant, saying: ﴿Indeed, they, when it was said to them, "There is no god but Allah," were arrogant﴾, and He said: ﴿When those who disbelieved put into their hearts zealotry, the zealotry of ignorance, then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers and made them adhere to the word of righteousness, and they were more deserving of it and worthy of it﴾ [al-Fath: 26]. It is the statement "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." The polytheists were arrogant toward it on the day of al-Hudaybiyya, the day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made the treaty with them for the term of truce.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th recorded from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿A cup from a flowing spring is passed around among them﴾, that he said: it is wine. ﴿No ghawl is in it﴾, he said: there is no headache in it. ﴿Nor are they intoxicated by it﴾, he said: their minds do not depart.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh recorded from him that he said regarding wine: it has four properties: intoxication, headache, vomiting, and urination. So Allah cleansed the wine of Paradise of them, saying: ﴿No ghawl is in it﴾, its minds are not seized by intoxication, ﴿nor are they intoxicated by it﴾, he said: they vomit from it as the owner of the wine of this world vomits from it.

Ibn Jarir recorded from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿No ghawl is in it﴾, he said: it is wine, there is no stomach ache in it.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th also recorded from him regarding His saying: ﴿And with them are those restraining their gaze﴾, he said: from other than their husbands. ﴿As if they were hidden eggs﴾, he said: hidden pearls.

Ibn al-Mundhir recorded from him regarding His saying: ﴿As if they were hidden eggs﴾, he said: the whiteness of the egg, from which its membrane and covering have been removed.

**Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 37, verses 20–49 (part 1 of 2)**

His words: ﴿They will say, "Woe to us!"﴾ That is, those who are resurrected will say, when they witness the Resurrection that they used to deny in the world: "Woe to us!" They call down woe upon themselves.

Al-Zajjaj said: "Al-waylu (woe) is a word that the speaker utters at the time of destruction." Al-Farra' said: "Its original form is *ya way lana*, and *way* means grief, as if he said: 'O grief for us!'"

Al-Nahhas said: "If it were as he said, it would have been written separately, but in the Mushaf it is written joined, and we know of no one who writes it except joined."

His words: ﴿This is the Day of Judgment﴾ is a justification for their calling woe upon themselves. *Al-din* means recompense. It is as if they said: "This is the day on which we will be recompensed for our deeds, of disbelief and denying the Messengers." The angels then answered them with their words: ﴿This is the Day of Decision, which you used to deny﴾. It is also permissible that this is the speech of some of them to others. *Al-fasl* means judgment and decree, because on that day a decision is made between the good-doer and the wrongdoer.

His words: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their spouses﴾ is a command from Allah, glorified is He, to the angels to gather the polytheists and their spouses, meaning those who resemble them in polytheism, who follow them in disbelief, and who support them in denying the Messengers. This is what Qatadah and Abu al-'Aliyah said.

Al-Hasan and Mujahid said: what is meant by "their spouses" is their polytheist wives who agreed with them in disbelief and wrongdoing.

Al-Dahhak said: "Their spouses are their companions from among the devils; every disbeliever is gathered with his devil." Muqatil also said this.

﴿And what they used to worship besides Allah﴾, from among the idols and the devils. This generality is derived from *ma* (the relative pronoun), since it refers to the things worshipped, not the worshippers. It is said to be restricted, because among the groups of disbelievers are those who worshipped the Messiah and those who worshipped the angels, and they are excluded by His words: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best (reward) has preceded from Us, they will be kept far from it﴾ [al-Anbiya': 101]. The reason for gathering the idols, even though they are inanimate and do not understand, is to increase the rebuke of their worshippers, to shame them, and to show that they neither benefit nor harm.

﴿So guide them to the path of Hellfire﴾, that is: make known to these gathered ones (p-1238) the way to the Fire and drive them toward it. It is said: *hadaytuhu al-tariq* and *hadaytuhu ilayha*, meaning I directed him to it. In this there is mockery of them.

﴿And stop them, for they are to be questioned﴾, that is: detain them. It is said: *waqaftu al-dabbah aqifuha waqfan*, and then *waqafat hiya wuqufan*, which is both transitive and intransitive. This detention occurs before they are driven to Hell, meaning: stop them for reckoning, then drive them to the Fire after that. The clause ﴿for they are to be questioned﴾ gives the reason for the first clause.

Al-Kalbi said: that is, they will be questioned about their deeds, their words, and their actions.

Al-Dahhak said: about their sins. It was also said: about "There is no god but Allah." It was also said: about wronging people. And it was also said: about wronging people.

It was said that this questioning is the one mentioned after this in His words: ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not help one another?﴾, that is: what is wrong with you that you do not help one another as you used to in the world? This is a rebuke, reproach, and mockery of them. Its original form is *tatanasarun*, and one of the two *ta'*s was dropped for lightness.

Al-Jumhur recited ﴿innahum mas'ulun﴾ with a kasrah on the hamzah. 'Isa ibn 'Umar recited it with a fathah.

Al-Kisa'i said: that is, "because they" or "that they." It was also said: the reference of His words ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not help one another?﴾ is to the words of Abu Jahl on the Day of Badr: ﴿We are a united company, victorious﴾ [al-Qamar: 44].

Then He, glorified is He, turned from what preceded to explain the state they are in at that moment, so He said: ﴿Rather, they are today in submission﴾, that is: surrendering, because they are unable to find a way out. Qatadah said: "submitting to the punishment of Allah." Al-Akhfash said: "casting down their hands." It is said: *istaslama lil-shay'* when one yields to something and humbles himself before it.

﴿And some of them turn to others, questioning one another﴾, that is: some of the disbelievers turn to others, questioning one another. It was said: they are the followers and the leaders, who question one another with questions of rebuke, reproach, and contention. Mujahid said: it is the saying of the disbelievers to the devils. Qatadah said: it is the saying of humans to the jinn. The first view is preferable because of His words: ﴿They will say, "Indeed you used to come to us from the right."﴾, that is: you used to come to us in the world from the right, meaning from the direction of truth, religion, and obedience, and you would turn us away from them.

Al-Zajjaj said: "You used to come to us from the direction of religion, and you made us see that religion and truth were what you misled us with. *Al-yamin* is an expression for truth." This is like His words, exalted is He, reporting about Iblis: ﴿Then I will surely come to them from before them, from behind them, from their right and from their left﴾ [al-A'raf: 17].

Al-Wahidi said: The people of the meanings (scholars) said: the leaders had sworn to these followers that what they called them to was the truth, so the followers trusted their oaths. So the meaning of ﴿you used to come to us from the right﴾ is: from the side of the oaths which you used to swear, so we trusted them. He said: "But the exegetes hold the first view."

It was also said: the meaning is: you used to come to us from the right that we love and take as a good omen, so that you would entice us by it, presenting it as sincere counsel. The Arabs take as a good omen what comes from the right and call it *al-sanih*.

It was also said: *al-yamin* means strength, that is: you used to restrain us by force, dominance, and coercion, as in His words: ﴿So he turned upon them, striking with the right hand﴾ [al-Saffat: 93], meaning with strength. This sentence is a new clause answering an implied question.

Likewise the clause ﴿They will say, "Rather, you were not believers"﴾ is a new clause answering an implied question. The meaning is: the leaders or devils said to these speakers, "You used to come to us from the right": "Rather, you were not believers, and we did not prevent you from faith."

The meaning is: you were never believers until we moved you from faith to disbelief. Rather, you were from the outset upon disbelief, and you persisted in it.

﴿And we had no authority over you﴾, that is: no dominance by coercion or force, so that we could bring you into faith or take you out of disbelief. ﴿Rather, you were a transgressing people﴾, that is: going beyond the limit in disbelief and misguidance.

His words: ﴿So the word of our Lord has come into effect upon us. Indeed, we are to taste (the punishment)﴾ are the words of the followed, meaning: the word of our Lord has become binding upon us and upon you, and has obligated us. They mean His words, exalted is He: ﴿I will surely fill Hell with you and whoever follows you among them, all together﴾ [Sad: 85]. (Indeed, we are tasters of the punishment), that is: all of us are tasters of the punishment that was promised. Al-Zajjaj said: "That is, the misleader and the misled are both in the Fire."

﴿So we misled you﴾, that is: we led you astray from guidance, invited you to what we were in of error, and made what you were upon of disbelief seem fair to you. ﴿Indeed, we were ourselves erring﴾. So there is no blame upon us for our targeting you for misguidance, because we wanted you to be like us in going astray. The meaning of the verse is: we proceeded to mislead you because we ourselves were described as being in error. Here they acknowledge that they caused their misguidance, but not through force or domination, and they deny what they said earlier, that they had coerced and overpowered them, so they said: ﴿And we had no authority over you﴾.

Then Allah, glorified is He, reported about the followers and the followed with His words: ﴿Indeed, they on that Day will be sharers in the punishment﴾, just as they were sharers in misguidance.

﴿Indeed, that is how We deal with the criminals﴾, that is: We deal in the same way with the criminals, that is, the people of crime, who are the polytheists.

As His words indicate: ﴿Indeed, they, when it was said to them, "There is no god but Allah," would become arrogant﴾, that is: when they were told, "Say: There is no god but Allah," they became arrogant and refused to accept it. The place of *yastakbirun* is in the accusative as the predicate of *kana*, or in the nominative as the predicate of *inna*, and *kana* here is *mulgha* (cancelled, i.e., with no governing effect).

﴿And they say, "Shall we really leave our gods for a mad poet?"﴾ They mean the Prophet (ﷺ), that is: for the words of a mad poet. Allah, glorified is He, responded to them with His words: ﴿Rather, he has brought the truth﴾, meaning the Qur'an, which includes monotheism, promise, and warning, ﴿and confirmed the Messengers﴾, that is: he confirmed them in what they brought of monotheism, warning, and the affirmation of the Last Abode, and did not oppose them, nor did he bring anything that the Messengers before him had not brought.

﴿Indeed, you will surely taste the painful punishment﴾, that is: indeed, because of your polytheism and your denial, you will surely taste the severely painful punishment.

Al-Jumhur recited ﴿la-dha'iqu﴾ with the *nun* dropped and *al-'adhab* in the genitive. Aban ibn Tha'lab, on the authority of 'Asim, and Abu al-Simak recited it with the *nun* dropped and *al-'adhab* in the accusative. Sibawayh cited, as an example of this recitation with the dropped *nun* and the accusative for *al-'adhab*, the verse of the poet:

*So I found him not seeking to appease, nor remembering God except a little.*

Sibawayh also permitted *wal-muqimi al-salah* (al-Hajj: 35) with *al-salah* in the accusative on this analysis. It has also been recited with the *nun* retained and *al-'adhab* in the accusative, in accordance with the original form.

Then He, glorified is He, explained that what they tasted of punishment was only because of their deeds, so He said: ﴿And you are not recompensed except for what you used to do﴾, that is: you are recompensed only for what you used to do of disbelief and sins, or: only because of what you used to do.

Then He excepted the believers, saying: ﴿Except the chosen servants of Allah﴾. The people of Madinah and Kufah recited *al-mukhlasin* (p-1239) with a fathah on the *lam*, meaning: those whom Allah chose for His obedience and monotheism.

The rest recited it with a kasrah, meaning: those who made their worship and monotheism sincerely for Allah. The exception is either connected, on the assumption that the address in *tujzawna* ("you are recompensed") is general to all the responsible, or disconnected, meaning: but the chosen servants of Allah will not taste the punishment.

The reference of His words ﴿those﴾ is to the sincere ones, and it is the subject (*mubtada'*), whose predicate is His words: ﴿For them is a known provision﴾, that is: for these sincere ones is a provision which Allah provides for them, known in its goodness, its pleasantness, and its being unending.

Qatadah said: "That refers to Paradise." It was also said: "It is known in its time, namely that they will be given it morning and evening, as in His words: ﴿And for them is their provision therein, morning and evening﴾ [Maryam: 62]." It was also said: it is what is mentioned in His words after it.

﴿Fruits﴾: this is either a substitute (*badal*) for *rizq* (provision), or the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: it is fruits. This is the apparent meaning.

*Al-fawakih* is the plural of *al-fakihah*, which means all fruits, both fresh and dry. Fruits are singled out for mention because all the provisions of the people of Paradise are fruits, so it is said. But the better view is that they are singled out because they are the most delicious of what they eat and the most pleasing to their souls. It was also said: fruits are the accompaniment of all other foods, so mentioning them makes mention of others unnecessary.

His words: ﴿And they will be honored﴾ are in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (*hal*), meaning: they will receive from Allah, mighty and majestic is He, a great honor, by raising their ranks with Him, hearing His speech, and meeting Him in Paradise. Al-Jumhur recited *mukramun* with the *ra'* lightened. Abu Miqsam recited it with the *ra'* doubled.

His words: ﴿in the Gardens of Bliss﴾ may be connected to *mukramun*, or be a second predicate, or be a circumstantial clause.

His words: ﴿upon thrones﴾ may be a circumstantial clause, or a third predicate. The accusative of ﴿facing one another﴾ is a circumstantial clause from the pronoun in *mukramun*, or from the pronoun in the complement of "upon thrones."

Ikrimah and Mujahid said: the meaning of facing one another is that none of them looks at the back of another. It was also said: the thrones turn them around however they wish, so none of them sees the back of another.

Al-Jumhur recited *surur* (thrones) with a *damma* on the *ra'*. Abu al-Simak recited it with a fathah, which is the dialect of some of the Tamim tribe.

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned another attribute of theirs, saying: ﴿A cup from a flowing spring will be passed around to them﴾. This sentence may be a new clause answering an implied question, or it may be in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause from the pronoun in *mutaqabilin*. The *ka's* (cup), according to the lexicographers, is a term for any vessel containing drink, so if it is empty, it is not a *ka's*.

Al-Dahhak and al-Sudi said: every *ka's* in the Qur'an is wine.

Al-Nahhas said: "Some reliable lexicographers have reported that the Arabs call a goblet a *ka's* when it contains wine, but when it contains no wine it is a *qadah* (bowl), just as a tray is called *ma'ida* when it has food on it, and if it has no food on it, it is not called *ma'ida*." And ﴿from a flowing spring﴾ is connected to an omitted word which is an attribute of *ka's*.

**Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 37, verses 20–49 (part 2 of 2):**

Al-Zajjaj said: ﴿with a cup from a flowing spring﴾ means: from wine that flows as springs flow over the surface of the earth. *Ma'in* is flowing water.

His saying ﴿white, delicious to the drinkers﴾ are two attributes of *ka's* (cup).

Al-Zajjaj said: that is, *dhat ladhdha* (possessing deliciousness), so the noun modified was omitted. It is also permissible for the attribute to be the verbal noun *ladhdha* (delight) for the sake of emphasis on its being pure delight, so there is no need to posit an omitted noun.

Al-Hasan said: The wine of Paradise is whiter than milk and has a delicious taste. It is said: *sharab ladhdh* and *sharab ladhidh* (a delightful drink), just as it is said: *nabat ghadd* and *ghadid* (tender plant). From this is the saying of the poet:

*"With her sweet speech, which, if she spoke to the lions of the desert with it, they would come swiftly."*

*Al-ladhidh* is everything that is found pleasant. It was also said: *al-bayda'* is the one that men have not pressed.

Then He described this cup of wine by what differs from the wine of this world, saying: ﴿No ghawl is in it﴾, meaning: it does not seize their minds so as to carry them away, and no illness or headache afflicts them from it. ﴿Nor are they intoxicated by it﴾, meaning: they do not become drunk. It is said: *nazafa al-sharib* so he is *manzuf* and *nazif* when he becomes drunk. From this is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

*"And when she walks, like the walk of the nazif, she is overcome by the breathlessness among the sand dunes."*

He also said:

*"A nazif, when she stands for a face, sways."*

From this is the saying of another:

*"So I kissed her mouth, seizing her horns, drinking like the nazif with the cold water of al-Hashraj."*

Al-Farra' said: The Arabs say *laysa fiha ghilah wa ghā'ila wa ghawl* (there is no ghilah, ghā'ila, or ghawl in it), all meaning the same.

Abu Ubayda said: *al-ghawl* is that it seizes their minds. He cited the verse of Mut'i' ibn Iyas:

*"The cup did not cease to seize them, and to take away the first and the foremost."*

Al-Wahidi said: The essential meaning of *al-ghawl* is destruction. It is said: *ghālahu ghawlan* and *ightālahu*, meaning he destroyed him. *Al-ghawl* is everything that seizes you, i.e., destroys you.

The majority of readers recited ﴿yunzafun﴾ with a *dammah* on the *ya'* and a *fatha* on the *za'*, in the passive voice.

Hamza and al-Kisa'i recited it with a *dammah* on the *ya'* and a *kasra* on the *za'*, from *anzafa al-rajul*, when his mind departed due to drunkenness, so he is *nazif*, *manzuf*, and *munzif*. It is said: *ahsud al-zar'* when its harvest has come, and *aqtif al-karm* when its gathering has come.

Al-Farra' said: Whoever recites with a *kasra* on the *za'* has two meanings: it is said *anzafa al-rajul* when his wine has run out, and *anzafa* when his mind has departed due to drunkenness. This reading may be understood to mean that their drink does not run out, for the sake of added benefit.

Al-Nahhas said: The first reading is clearer and more correct in meaning, because the meaning of ﴿la yunzafun﴾ according to the majority of the exegetes is: their minds do not depart. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, negated from the wine of Paradise the afflictions that befall the wine of this world, from headache and intoxication.

Al-Zajjaj and Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said that the meaning of *la yanzifun* with a *kasra* on the *za'* is: they do not become drunk.

Al-Mahdawi said: The meaning of *yunzafun* cannot be "they become drunk," because before it is ﴿no ghawl is in it﴾, i.e., it does not seize their minds, so it would be a repetition. This supports what Qatada said: that *al-ghawl* is stomach ache, and so Ibn Abi Najih narrated from Mujahid. Al-Hasan said: *al-ghawl* is headache. Ibn Kaysan said: it is colic. So the meaning of the verse is: there is in it no kind of corruption that accompanies the drinking of wine in this world, whether colic, stomach ache, headache, rowdiness, idle talk, or sinfulness, and they are not drunk from it.

This is supported by the fact that the origin of *al-ghawl* is corruption that strikes in secret. It is said: *ightālahu ightiyālan* when he corrupted his affair in secret. From this comes *al-ghawl* and *al-ghīla*, killing in secret.

Ibn Abi Ishaq recited ﴿yunzifun﴾ with a *fatha* on the *ya'* and a *kasra* on the *za'*.

Talha ibn Musarrif recited it with a *fatha* on the *ya'* and a *dammah* on the *za'*.

When He, glorified be He, mentioned the description of their drink, He mentioned right after it the description of their spouses, saying: ﴿And with them are those restraining their gaze﴾, meaning: women who restrain their gaze to their husbands, so they do not desire others. *Al-qasr* means confinement, and from this is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

*"Of the women restraining the gaze, if a tiny ant crawled upon her shirt, it would leave a mark."*

*Al-muhwil* is the small ant, and *al-itb* is the shirt. It was said: *al-qasirat* are those confined to their husbands. The first is preferable, because He said *qasirat al-tarf* and did not say *maqsurat*.

*Al-'in* is the plural of *'ayna'*, which is the woman with large eyes.

Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of *'in* is large eyes and beautiful ones. Mujahid said: *al-'in* are those with beautiful eyes.

Al-Hasan said: They are those who have intense whiteness of the eye and intense blackness of it, and the first is preferable.

﴿As if they were hidden eggs﴾. Al-Hasan and Abu Zayd said: He likened them to ostrich eggs which the ostrich covers with feathers from the wind and dust, so their color is white tinged with yellow, which is the most beautiful of women's colors.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi said: He likened them to the inner part of the egg before it is peeled and touched by hands, and Ibn Jarir also said this. From this is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

*"And an egg of a curtained tent, whose tent is not approached, I enjoyed from play with her without haste."*

Al-Mubarrad said: The Arabs say, when they describe a thing with beauty and cleanliness, "as if it were ostrich eggs covered with feathers."

It was also said: *al-maknun* is the one protected from breaking, meaning they are virgins. It was also said: the intended *al-bayd* is pearls, as in His saying: ﴿And wide-eyed maidens, like hidden pearls﴾ [al-Waqi'a: 22–23]. Similar to this is the saying of the poet:

*"And she is white like a pearl of al-Ghawwas, distinguished from a hidden jewel."*

The first is preferable. He said *maknun* and did not say *maknunat*, because He described the eggs in respect of the wording.

Ibn Abi Hatim recorded from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their spouses﴾, that he said: The angels say this saying to the guards of Hell.

Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Ibn Abi Shayba, Ibn Mani' in his Musnad, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th recorded through the route of al-Nu'man ibn Bashir from Umar ibn al-Khattab regarding His saying: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their spouses﴾, that he said: their likes, those who are like them: the people of usury come with the people of usury, the people of fornication with the people of fornication, and the people of wine with the people of wine, spouses in Paradise and spouses in the Fire.

Al-Firyabi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shayba, Ibn al-Mundhir, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th recorded from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their spouses﴾, that he said: their likes, and in another wording: their counterparts.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim recorded from him regarding His saying: ﴿So guide them to the path of Hellfire﴾, that he said: direct them. Ibn Abi Hatim also recorded from him in the verse, he said: guide them ﴿to the path of Hellfire﴾, he said: the path of the Fire.

He also recorded from him regarding His saying: ﴿And stop them, indeed they are to be questioned﴾, that he said: hold them, indeed they are to be called to account.

Al-Bukhari in his History, al-Darimi, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), and Ibn Mardawayh recorded from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is no caller who calls to something except that he will be made to stand with it on the Day of Resurrection, bound to it, never separating from it, even if a man calls a man." Then he recited: ﴿And stop them, indeed they are to be questioned﴾.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim recorded from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And some of them will turn to others, questioning one another﴾, that he said: that is when they are raised at the second blast.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh recorded from him regarding His saying: ﴿When it was said to them, "There is no god but Allah," they became arrogant﴾, that he said: they were disdainful when no partner was associated with Allah. ﴿And they say, "Shall we really leave our gods for a mad poet?"﴾, which is not sensible. He said: Allah related his truthfulness, so He said: ﴿Rather, he has brought the truth and confirmed the messengers﴾.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat recorded from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have been commanded to fight the people until they say 'There is no god but Allah.' Whoever says 'There is no god but Allah' has protected his property and his life from me, except by its right, and his account is with Allah."

Allah revealed in His Book, mentioning a people who were arrogant, saying: ﴿Indeed, they, when it was said to them, "There is no god but Allah," were arrogant﴾, and He said: ﴿When those who disbelieved put into their hearts zealotry, the zealotry of ignorance, then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers and made them adhere to the word of righteousness, and they were more deserving of it and worthy of it﴾ [al-Fath: 26]. It is the statement "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." The polytheists were arrogant toward it on the day of al-Hudaybiyya, the day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made the treaty with them for the term of truce.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th recorded from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿A cup from a flowing spring is passed around among them﴾, that he said: it is wine. ﴿No ghawl is in it﴾, he said: there is no headache in it. ﴿Nor are they intoxicated by it﴾, he said: their minds do not depart.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh recorded from him that he said regarding wine: it has four properties: intoxication, headache, vomiting, and urination. So Allah cleansed the wine of Paradise of them, saying: ﴿No ghawl is in it﴾, its minds are not seized by intoxication, ﴿nor are they intoxicated by it﴾, he said: they vomit from it as the owner of the wine of this world vomits from it.

Ibn Jarir recorded from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿No ghawl is in it﴾, he said: it is wine, there is no stomach ache in it.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th also recorded from him regarding His saying: ﴿And with them are those restraining their gaze﴾, he said: from other than their husbands. ﴿As if they were hidden eggs﴾, he said: hidden pearls.

Ibn al-Mundhir recorded from him regarding His saying: ﴿As if they were hidden eggs﴾, he said: the whiteness of the egg, from which its membrane and covering have been removed.

**Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 37, verses 20–49 (part 1 of 2)**

His words: ﴿They will say, "Woe to us!"﴾ That is, those who are resurrected will say, when they witness the Resurrection that they used to deny in the world: "Woe to us!" They call down woe upon themselves.

Al-Zajjaj said: "Al-waylu (woe) is a word that the speaker utters at the time of destruction." Al-Farra' said: "Its original form is *ya way lana*, and *way* means grief, as if he said: 'O grief for us!'"

Al-Nahhas said: "If it were as he said, it would have been written separately, but in the Mushaf it is written joined, and we know of no one who writes it except joined."

His words: ﴿This is the Day of Judgment﴾ is a justification for their calling woe upon themselves. *Al-din* means recompense. It is as if they said: "This is the day on which we will be recompensed for our deeds, of disbelief and denying the Messengers." The angels then answered them with their words: ﴿This is the Day of Decision, which you used to deny﴾. It is also permissible that this is the speech of some of them to others. *Al-fasl* means judgment and decree, because on that day a decision is made between the good-doer and the wrongdoer.

His words: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their spouses﴾ is a command from Allah, glorified is He, to the angels to gather the polytheists and their spouses, meaning those who resemble them in polytheism, who follow them in disbelief, and who support them in denying the Messengers. This is what Qatadah and Abu al-'Aliyah said.

Al-Hasan and Mujahid said: what is meant by "their spouses" is their polytheist wives who agreed with them in disbelief and wrongdoing.

Al-Dahhak said: "Their spouses are their companions from among the devils; every disbeliever is gathered with his devil." Muqatil also said this.

﴿And what they used to worship besides Allah﴾, from among the idols and the devils. This generality is derived from *ma* (the relative pronoun), since it refers to the things worshipped, not the worshippers. It is said to be restricted, because among the groups of disbelievers are those who worshipped the Messiah and those who worshipped the angels, and they are excluded by His words: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best (reward) has preceded from Us, they will be kept far from it﴾ [al-Anbiya': 101]. The reason for gathering the idols, even though they are inanimate and do not understand, is to increase the rebuke of their worshippers, to shame them, and to show that they neither benefit nor harm.

﴿So guide them to the path of Hellfire﴾, that is: make known to these gathered ones (p-1238) the way to the Fire and drive them toward it. It is said: *hadaytuhu al-tariq* and *hadaytuhu ilayha*, meaning I directed him to it. In this there is mockery of them.

﴿And stop them, for they are to be questioned﴾, that is: detain them. It is said: *waqaftu al-dabbah aqifuha waqfan*, and then *waqafat hiya wuqufan*, which is both transitive and intransitive. This detention occurs before they are driven to Hell, meaning: stop them for reckoning, then drive them to the Fire after that. The clause ﴿for they are to be questioned﴾ gives the reason for the first clause.

Al-Kalbi said: that is, they will be questioned about their deeds, their words, and their actions.

Al-Dahhak said: about their sins. It was also said: about "There is no god but Allah." It was also said: about wronging people. And it was also said: about wronging people.

It was said that this questioning is the one mentioned after this in His words: ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not help one another?﴾, that is: what is wrong with you that you do not help one another as you used to in the world? This is a rebuke, reproach, and mockery of them. Its original form is *tatanasarun*, and one of the two *ta'*s was dropped for lightness.

Al-Jumhur recited ﴿innahum mas'ulun﴾ with a kasrah on the hamzah. 'Isa ibn 'Umar recited it with a fathah.

Al-Kisa'i said: that is, "because they" or "that they." It was also said: the reference of His words ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not help one another?﴾ is to the words of Abu Jahl on the Day of Badr: ﴿We are a united company, victorious﴾ [al-Qamar: 44].

Then He, glorified is He, turned from what preceded to explain the state they are in at that moment, so He said: ﴿Rather, they are today in submission﴾, that is: surrendering, because they are unable to find a way out. Qatadah said: "submitting to the punishment of Allah." Al-Akhfash said: "casting down their hands." It is said: *istaslama lil-shay'* when one yields to something and humbles himself before it.

﴿And some of them turn to others, questioning one another﴾, that is: some of the disbelievers turn to others, questioning one another. It was said: they are the followers and the leaders, who question one another with questions of rebuke, reproach, and contention. Mujahid said: it is the saying of the disbelievers to the devils. Qatadah said: it is the saying of humans to the jinn. The first view is preferable because of His words: ﴿They will say, "Indeed you used to come to us from the right."﴾, that is: you used to come to us in the world from the right, meaning from the direction of truth, religion, and obedience, and you would turn us away from them.

Al-Zajjaj said: "You used to come to us from the direction of religion, and you made us see that religion and truth were what you misled us with. *Al-yamin* is an expression for truth." This is like His words, exalted is He, reporting about Iblis: ﴿Then I will surely come to them from before them, from behind them, from their right and from their left﴾ [al-A'raf: 17].

Al-Wahidi said: The people of the meanings (scholars) said: the leaders had sworn to these followers that what they called them to was the truth, so the followers trusted their oaths. So the meaning of ﴿you used to come to us from the right﴾ is: from the side of the oaths which you used to swear, so we trusted them. He said: "But the exegetes hold the first view."

It was also said: the meaning is: you used to come to us from the right that we love and take as a good omen, so that you would entice us by it, presenting it as sincere counsel. The Arabs take as a good omen what comes from the right and call it *al-sanih*.

It was also said: *al-yamin* means strength, that is: you used to restrain us by force, dominance, and coercion, as in His words: ﴿So he turned upon them, striking with the right hand﴾ [al-Saffat: 93], meaning with strength. This sentence is a new clause answering an implied question.

Likewise the clause ﴿They will say, "Rather, you were not believers"﴾ is a new clause answering an implied question. The meaning is: the leaders or devils said to these speakers, "You used to come to us from the right": "Rather, you were not believers, and we did not prevent you from faith."

The meaning is: you were never believers until we moved you from faith to disbelief. Rather, you were from the outset upon disbelief, and you persisted in it.

﴿And we had no authority over you﴾, that is: no dominance by coercion or force, so that we could bring you into faith or take you out of disbelief. ﴿Rather, you were a transgressing people﴾, that is: going beyond the limit in disbelief and misguidance.

His words: ﴿So the word of our Lord has come into effect upon us. Indeed, we are to taste (the punishment)﴾ are the words of the followed, meaning: the word of our Lord has become binding upon us and upon you, and has obligated us. They mean His words, exalted is He: ﴿I will surely fill Hell with you and whoever follows you among them, all together﴾ [Sad: 85]. (Indeed, we are tasters of the punishment), that is: all of us are tasters of the punishment that was promised. Al-Zajjaj said: "That is, the misleader and the misled are both in the Fire."

﴿So we misled you﴾, that is: we led you astray from guidance, invited you to what we were in of error, and made what you were upon of disbelief seem fair to you. ﴿Indeed, we were ourselves erring﴾. So there is no blame upon us for our targeting you for misguidance, because we wanted you to be like us in going astray. The meaning of the verse is: we proceeded to mislead you because we ourselves were described as being in error. Here they acknowledge that they caused their misguidance, but not through force or domination, and they deny what they said earlier, that they had coerced and overpowered them, so they said: ﴿And we had no authority over you﴾.

Then Allah, glorified is He, reported about the followers and the followed with His words: ﴿Indeed, they on that Day will be sharers in the punishment﴾, just as they were sharers in misguidance.

﴿Indeed, that is how We deal with the criminals﴾, that is: We deal in the same way with the criminals, that is, the people of crime, who are the polytheists.

As His words indicate: ﴿Indeed, they, when it was said to them, "There is no god but Allah," would become arrogant﴾, that is: when they were told, "Say: There is no god but Allah," they became arrogant and refused to accept it. The place of *yastakbirun* is in the accusative as the predicate of *kana*, or in the nominative as the predicate of *inna*, and *kana* here is *mulgha* (cancelled, i.e., with no governing effect).

﴿And they say, "Shall we really leave our gods for a mad poet?"﴾ They mean the Prophet (ﷺ), that is: for the words of a mad poet. Allah, glorified is He, responded to them with His words: ﴿Rather, he has brought the truth﴾, meaning the Qur'an, which includes monotheism, promise, and warning, ﴿and confirmed the Messengers﴾, that is: he confirmed them in what they brought of monotheism, warning, and the affirmation of the Last Abode, and did not oppose them, nor did he bring anything that the Messengers before him had not brought.

﴿Indeed, you will surely taste the painful punishment﴾, that is: indeed, because of your polytheism and your denial, you will surely taste the severely painful punishment.

Al-Jumhur recited ﴿la-dha'iqu﴾ with the *nun* dropped and *al-'adhab* in the genitive. Aban ibn Tha'lab, on the authority of 'Asim, and Abu al-Simak recited it with the *nun* dropped and *al-'adhab* in the accusative. Sibawayh cited, as an example of this recitation with the dropped *nun* and the accusative for *al-'adhab*, the verse of the poet:

*So I found him not seeking to appease, nor remembering God except a little.*

Sibawayh also permitted *wal-muqimi al-salah* (al-Hajj: 35) with *al-salah* in the accusative on this analysis. It has also been recited with the *nun* retained and *al-'adhab* in the accusative, in accordance with the original form.

Then He, glorified is He, explained that what they tasted of punishment was only because of their deeds, so He said: ﴿And you are not recompensed except for what you used to do﴾, that is: you are recompensed only for what you used to do of disbelief and sins, or: only because of what you used to do.

Then He excepted the believers, saying: ﴿Except the chosen servants of Allah﴾. The people of Madinah and Kufah recited *al-mukhlasin* (p-1239) with a fathah on the *lam*, meaning: those whom Allah chose for His obedience and monotheism.

The rest recited it with a kasrah, meaning: those who made their worship and monotheism sincerely for Allah. The exception is either connected, on the assumption that the address in *tujzawna* ("you are recompensed") is general to all the responsible, or disconnected, meaning: but the chosen servants of Allah will not taste the punishment.

The reference of His words ﴿those﴾ is to the sincere ones, and it is the subject (*mubtada'*), whose predicate is His words: ﴿For them is a known provision﴾, that is: for these sincere ones is a provision which Allah provides for them, known in its goodness, its pleasantness, and its being unending.
