Tha'lab said: People differed concerning His, glorified be He, saying "Ba'l". One group said: Ba'l here is the idol; another group said: Ba'l here is an angel; and Ibn Ishaq said: it is a woman they used to worship.

Al-Wahidi said: the exegetes say it means "lord" (rabban), and it is in the dialect of Yemen, where they call the master and the lord "ba'l".

Al-Nahhas said: both sayings are correct, i.e., do you call upon an idol that you made a lord ﴿and leave the best of creators﴾, i.e., and you abandon worshipping the best of those who are called "creator".

The noble name in His saying ﴿Allah, your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers of old﴾ is in the accusative as a substitution (badal) for "the best", and this is according to the reading of Hamza, al-Kisa'i, al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Yahya ibn Wathhab and al-A'mash, for they read all three names in the accusative. It was also said: the accusative is by way of praise (madh), and it was said: by way of explicative apposition ('atf al-bayan). Abu 'Ubayd related that the accusative is by way of description (na't).

Al-Nahhas said: This is an error; it is rather a substitution, and description is not permissible because it is not an ornamental qualifier. Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred this reading.

Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, 'Asim, Abu Ja'far, Shayba and Nafi' read in the nominative.

Abu Hatim said: with the meaning "He is Allah, your Lord." Al-Nahhas said: the best that has been said is that it is a subject and predicate without any supposition or omission. It is related from al-Akhfash that the nominative is preferable and better. Ibn al-Anbari said: whoever reads in the nominative or the accusative does not stop at "the best of creators" as a complete pause, because Allah is an apposition for "the best of creators" in both readings, and the meaning is that He is your creator and the creator of those before you, so He is the one who deserves worship.

﴿But they denied him, so they will surely be brought forth﴾, i.e., because of their denial of him they will indeed be brought forth into punishment. It has already been mentioned that the unrestricted sense of "bringing forth" is specific to evil.

﴿Except the chosen servants of Allah﴾, i.e., those among his people who were believers in Him. It is read with a kasra and a fatha on the lam, as has preceded. The meaning on the reading with kasra is that they devoted themselves sincerely to Allah, and on the reading with fatha is that Allah selected them from among His servants. Its explanation has already been given.

﴿And We left for him among the later generations: "Peace be upon the family of Yasin"﴾. Nafi', Ibn 'Amir, al-A'raj and Shayba read "'ala Al Yasin" with "Al" construed to "Yasin", meaning "the family of Yasin." The rest read with a kasra on the hamza and a sakin on the lam, joined with "Yasin" — (p-1250) except al-Hasan, who read "al-Yasin" with the definite article attached to "Yasin." It was said: the intended meaning in all these readings is Ilyas, and upon this the salutation has fallen, but it is a non-Arabic name, and the Arabs vary greatly in these non-Arabic names and often alter them.

Ibn Jinni said: The Arabs play with non-Arabic names in a variety of ways; so "Yasin," "Ilyas," and "Ilyasin" are one and the same thing.

Al-Akhfash said: The Arabs name a man's people by the name of the outstanding man among them, so they say "al-Mahalibah," meaning they named every man among them after al-Muhallab. He said: On this basis, he named each man among them "al-Yasin."

Al-Farra' said: "al-Yasin" may be taken as a plural, so that his companions are included within his name.

Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said: its underlying form is "al-Yasiyin," with the two ya's of the relative construction deleted, as they are deleted in "al-Ash'arin" and "al-A'jamin."

Al-Farra' and Abu 'Ubayda preferred the reading of the majority, saying: "He did not say in any of the surahs 'upon the family of so-and-so'; rather the name came as it is, and 'al-Yasin' is the same, since it means Ilyas or Ilyas and his followers."

Al-Kalbi said: The intended meaning of "the family of Yasin" is the family of Muhammad.

Al-Wahidi said: This is far-fetched, because what follows it and what precedes it in the discourse does not indicate it.

The explanation of ﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the good-doers. Indeed, he was among Our believing servants﴾ has already been given in full.

﴿And indeed Lut was among the messengers﴾. The story of Lut has already been mentioned in full.

﴿When We delivered him and his family, all of them﴾. The temporal clause is connected to an omitted verb, which is "remember," and it is not correct for it to be connected to "the messengers," because he was not sent at the time of his deliverance.

﴿Except an old woman among those who remained behind﴾. It has already been stated that "al-ghabir" may mean "past" and may mean "remaining," so the meaning is: except an old woman among those who remained behind in the punishment, or among those who passed away and were destroyed.

﴿Then We destroyed the others﴾, i.e., We annihilated them with punishment. The meaning is that in his deliverance and that of his family all together, except the old woman, and the destruction of the rest of his people who did not believe in him, there is a clear proof of the establishment of his being one of the messengers.

﴿And indeed you pass by them in the morning﴾. With this He addressed the Arabs, or the people of Makkah specifically, i.e., you pass by their dwellings in which are the traces of punishment at morning time.

﴿And by night﴾. The meaning: you pass by their dwellings on your journey to Syria and your return from it, by day and by night. ﴿Will you not then reason?﴾ — regarding what you witness in their dwellings of the traces of Allah's punishment that descended upon them, for in that is a lesson for those who take heed and an admonition for those who reflect.

﴿And indeed Yunus was among the messengers﴾. Yunus is Dhu al-Nun, and he is the son of Matta.

The exegetes said: Yunus had promised his people punishment, and when the punishment was delayed from them, he went out from among them, intending the sea, and boarded a ship. By his going to the sea he was like one fleeing from his master, so he was described as a runaway (ibaq), and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿When he fled to the laden ship﴾. The origin of "ibaq" is fleeing from a master, but since his flight from his people was without the permission of his Lord, he was described by it.

Al-Mubarrad said: the interpretation of "abaqa" is "ba'ada," i.e., he went far away, and from this comes the saying "abd abiq" (a runaway slave).

The people of knowledge have differed on whether his prophethood was before the fish swallowed him or after. The meaning of "mashhun" is "filled."

﴿So he drew lots and was among the losers﴾. Al-musahama originally means contest, and it is casting lots, which is that the arrow falls upon the one who loses. Al-Mubarrad said: i.e., he cast lots. He said: its origin is from the arrows that are shuffled. The meaning of ﴿was among the losers﴾ is that he became one of the defeated.

He said: It is said: "his argument was refuted (dahadat hujjatuhu), and Allah refuted it," and its origin is from slipping from the place of a grip. From this is the poet's saying:

"We slew the refuted ones in every ravine, and the eyes were cooled by their slaughter."

i.e., the defeated.

﴿Then the fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy﴾. It is said: "laqimtu al-luqmah" and "altaqamtuha" when I swallowed it, i.e., the fish swallowed him. The meaning of ﴿while he was blameworthy﴾ is that he was deserving of blame. It is said: "rajul mulim" when he does something for which he is blamed; but "malum" is one who is blamed whether or not he does what deserves blame. It was said: "mulim" means "faulted," from "alama al-rajul" when he did something by which he became faulted.

The meaning of this lottery is that when Yunus boarded the ship it was held back, so the sailors said: "Here is a slave who has run away from his master, and this is the custom of a ship: when there is a runaway in it, it does not sail." So they cast lots, and the lot fell upon Yunus, and he said: "I am the runaway," and he threw himself into the water.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: When they cast lots, a fish came to the ship with its mouth open, awaiting the command of its Lord, until when he threw himself into the water the fish seized him.

﴿Had he not been among those who glorify (Allah)﴾, i.e., those who remember Allah or those who pray to Him.

﴿He would have remained in its belly until the Day they are resurrected﴾, i.e., the belly of the fish would have been a grave for him until the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: he would have remained in its belly alive.

The exegetes differed on how long he remained in the belly of the fish. Al-Suddi, al-Kalbi and Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: forty days. Al-Dahhak said: twenty days. 'Ata' said: seven days. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: three days. It was also said: one hour.

In this verse there is encouragement to the remembrance of Allah and an invigoration for those who remember Him.

﴿So We cast him onto the open plain while he was ill﴾. Nabdh means to throw down.

Al-'Ara': Ibn al-A'rabi said: it is the desert. Al-Akhfash said: the open space. Abu 'Ubayda said: the wide expanse of land. Al-Farra' said: the empty place.

It is also related from Abu 'Ubayda that he said: it is the surface of the earth, and he recited for a man from Khuza'ah:

"I raised a leg whose stumbling I do not fear, and I cast my garments in the land of al-'ara'."

The meaning is that Allah threw him from the belly of the fish onto the wide desert where there is no vegetation, and he was ill at the time of his casting because of the harm he had suffered in the belly of the fish. It was said: his body became like the body of a child at birth.

Some exegetes found it problematic to reconcile what occurred here, His saying ﴿So We cast him onto the open plain﴾, with His saying elsewhere: ﴿Had it not been that a blessing from his Lord had overtaken him, he would have been cast onto the open plain while blameworthy﴾ [al-Qalam: 49], for this verse indicates that he was not cast onto the open plain.

Al-Nahhas and others answered: Allah, glorified be He, here informs that he was cast onto the open plain while not blameworthy, and had it not been for His mercy, mighty and majestic, he would have been cast onto the open plain while blameworthy.

﴿And We caused a gourd plant to grow over him﴾, i.e., a tree above him that shaded him. It was also said: the meaning of "over him" is "near him"; and it was said: the meaning of "over him" is "for him."

Al-yaqtin is the gourd plant. Al-Mubarrad said: "yaqtin" is said of every plant that has no stalk but spreads over the surface of the earth, like the gourd, the watermelon and the colocynth; but if it has a stalk that carries it, it is called simply a tree. This is the saying of al-Hasan, Muqatil and others.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is everything that grows and then dies within its year. Al-Jawhari said: al-yaqtin is the kind of tree that has no stem, like the gourd plant and similar plants.

Al-Zajjaj said: the derivation of al-yaqtin is from qatana bi-l-makan, meaning he stayed in the place, so it is on the pattern of yaf'il. It was also said that it is a non-Arabic word.

The exegetes (al-mufassirun) said: he would shelter from the sun under its shade. Allah appointed for him a doe from the wild animals, which would come to him morning and evening. He would drink from its milk until his flesh grew firm and his hair grew, and then Allah sent him after that. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more.﴾ They were his people, from whom he had fled to the sea, and what happened to him after his flight happened, as Allah related it to us in this surah. They were the people of Nineveh.

Qatada said: he was sent to the people of Nineveh, from the land of Mosul. The account of his story has already been discussed in full in the surah of Yunus. As for the "or" (aw) in ﴿or more﴾, it was said: it has the meaning of "and" (waw), so the meaning is: "and more."

Al-Farra' said: "or" (aw) here means "rather" (bal), and this is the view of Muqatil and al-Kalbi.

Al-Mubarrad, al-Zajjaj and al-Akhfash said: "or" here remains on its original meaning, and the meaning is: "or more, in your estimation, when one who sees them says: 'These are a hundred thousand or more.'" So the doubt entered only into the reporting of the words of the created beings.

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: they were more by twenty thousand. Al-Hasan said: by some thirty thousand. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: seventy thousand.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad read "wa-yazidun" without the alif of doubt.

Scholars of tafsir differed as to whether this sending mentioned here was the one that came before the fish swallowed him, so that the waw in "wa-arsalnahu" would be merely for joining what happened to him with the fish and his sending to his people, without regard to the order of what came first and what came later in the context. Or it is a sending after what happened to him with the fish, according to two views. We have already pointed to the disagreement among the scholars as to whether he had been sent before he fled from his people to the sea, or whether he was not sent until after that. The preferred view is that he was a messenger before he went to the sea, as is indicated by what we mentioned in the surah of Yunus, and he continued in the message. The sending mentioned here is after his prophethood and his messengership had already preceded.

﴿So they believed, and We gave them enjoyment for a time.﴾ That is: belief occurred from them after they had witnessed the signs of his prophethood, so Allah gave them enjoyment in this world until the end of their appointed terms and the limit of their lifespans.

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Asakir reported from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "Ilyas is Idris." Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir reported from Qatada something similar.

Ibn Mardawayh reported from Ibn Abbas that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Al-Khadir is Ilyas."

Al-Hakim, who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il, who declared it weak, reported from Anas, who said: "We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a journey. He halted at a stopping place, and there was a man in the valley saying: 'O Allah, make me one of the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), the merciful, the forgiven, the one who is rewarded by it.' I looked over the valley, and its length was eighty cubits or more. He said: 'Who are you?' I said: 'Anas, the servant of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' He said: 'Where is he?' I said: 'He is here, listening to your speech.' He said: 'Go to him, convey my greetings to him, and say to him: Your brother Ilyas sends you his greetings.' So I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him, and he came until he embraced him, and they sat talking. He said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, I only eat one day in each year, and this is the day of my breaking the fast, so eat with me.' Then a table was sent down to them from heaven: bread, fish and celery. They both ate, and they fed me, and they prayed the afternoon prayer. Then he bade him farewell, and then I saw him passing over the clouds toward the sky."

Al-Dhahabi, commenting on al-Hakim's authentication of it, said: "Rather it is fabricated; may Allah curse the one who fabricated it."

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir reported from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿Do you call upon Ba'l?﴾, that he said: "An idol."

Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh reported from him, regarding His words "Peace be upon the family of Yasin," that he said: "We are the family of Muhammad, the family of Yasin."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Allah sent Yunus to the people of his town, and they rejected what he brought them and refused it. When they did that, Allah revealed to them: 'I am sending upon them the punishment on such-and-such a day.' He was taken out from among them, and he informed his people of the punishment which Allah had promised to inflict upon them. They said: 'Watch him. If he leaves from among you, then by Allah, what he has promised you will certainly come.' When the night came in which they had been promised the punishment, and in its morning, he set out by night, and the people saw him and were wary, so they went out of the town into an open area of their land, and they separated every animal from its young. Then they cried out to Allah and turned in repentance, and they asked for pardon, and Allah pardoned them. Yunus waited for news of the town and its people until a passer-by came to him, and he said: 'What has become of the people of the town?' He said: 'When their prophet went out from among them, they knew that he had spoken truly about the punishment he had promised them, so they went out of their town into an open area, and then they separated every creature with young from its young, then they cried out to Allah and repented to Him, so He accepted from them and deferred the punishment from them.' Then Yunus said at that: 'I will never return to them as a liar, ever,' and he went off in his own direction." We have already discussed his story and what has been related about it in the surah of Yunus, so we will not repeat it.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi reported from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and he cast lots﴾, that he said: "He drew lots." ﴿And he was among those who were overcome﴾: "Those who lost the drawing."

Ibn Abi Shayba, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from him, regarding His words ﴿and he was blameworthy﴾, that he said: "Blameworthy: one who had done wrong."

Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Ahmad in al-Zuhd, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from him, regarding His words ﴿Had he not been one of those who glorify Allah﴾, that he said: "One of those who pray."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from him, regarding His words ﴿Had he not been one of those who glorify Allah﴾, that he said: "One of those who pray."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also reported from him, regarding His words ﴿So We cast him onto the open shore﴾, that he said: "We threw him onto the shore."

These same reporters also reported from him, regarding His words ﴿a gourd plant﴾, that he said: "The gourd."

Ibn Abi Shayba and Ibn al-Mundhir reported through the chain of Sa'id ibn Jubayr from him, who said: "Al-yaqtin is everything that spreads over the surface of the earth."

Ahmad in al-Zuhd, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh reported from him, who said: "The mission of Yunus was only after the fish had cast him out. Then he recited: ﴿So We cast him onto the open shore﴾ up to His words ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand﴾." It has already been mentioned from him what indicates that his mission was before that. And there is nothing in the verse that indicates what he mentioned, as we have already said.

al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh reported from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: "I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the words of Allah: ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more,﴾ and he said: 'They were more by twenty thousand.'" Al-Tirmidhi said: "Gharib (a narration found through only a single line of transmission)."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn Abbas, who said: "They were more by thirty thousand."

It is also reported from him that they were more by some thirty-odd thousand, and it is also reported from him that they were more by some forty thousand. There is not much benefit in the disagreement about this.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 37, verse 114–148 (part 1 of 2):

When He, glorified be He, finished mentioning the rescue of the sacrificed one (dhabih) from the slaughter, and the favour He bestowed upon him afterward in prophethood, He mentioned what He bestowed upon Musa and Harun, saying: ﴿And We certainly bestowed favour upon Musa and Harun﴾, meaning with prophethood and other great blessings with which Allah graced them both.

﴿And We delivered them and their people from the great distress﴾. By "their people" is meant the believers among the Children of Israel, and by "the great distress" is meant what they were in of the enslavement by Pharaoh and the afflictions that befell them from him. It was also said that it is the drowning that destroyed Pharaoh and his people, but the first is more apt.

﴿And We helped them﴾ came with the pronoun of the plural. Al-Farra' said: the pronoun refers to Musa, Harun and their people, because before it is ﴿and We delivered them and their people﴾. The meaning of "help" is support for them against their enemy, so that by that means they became ﴿the victorious﴾ over their enemy, after they had been under their subjugation and domination. It was also said that the pronoun in "We helped them" refers to the two, Musa and Harun, as an honouring of them both, but the first is more apt.

﴿And We gave them both the clear Book﴾. By "the Book" is meant the Torah. Al-Mustabin means the clear and manifest; it is said: "istabana kadha", i.e., it became clear.

﴿And We guided them both to the straight path﴾, i.e., the upright, with no crookedness in it, and it is the religion of Islam, for it is the path that leads to the sought goal.

﴿And We left for them both among the later generations: "Peace be upon Musa and Harun"﴾, i.e., We preserved for them both among the later nations the good praise. We have already discussed the matter of "peace" and the grammatical reason for its being in the nominative case, and likewise its explanation has preceded.

﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the good-doers. Indeed, they both were among Our believing servants﴾ — this was explained in this surah.

﴿And indeed Ilyas was among the messengers﴾. The exegetes said: he was a prophet of the prophets of the Children of Israel, and his story with his people is well known. It was said: he is Ilyas son of Yasin, of the lineage of Harun, brother of Musa.

Ibn Ishaq and others said: Ilyas was the one in charge of the affairs of the Children of Israel after Yusha', and it was said: he is Idris, but the first is more apt.

The majority read "Ilyas" with a hamza of kasra that is cut (i.e., a separate hamza, qat'), and Ibn Dhakwan read it with a connected hamza (wasl), and this reading is narrated from Ibn 'Amir. Ibn Mas'ud, al-A'mash and Yahya ibn Wathhab read "wa-inna Idris la-mina al-mursalin". Ubayy read "wa-inna Iyilis" with a kasra-marked hamza, then a sakin ya', then a kasra-marked lam, then a sakin ya', then an unpointed sin with a fatha.

﴿When he said to his people: "Will you not be wary of God?"﴾. It is a temporal clause (zarf) governed by his saying "among the messengers", or it is connected to an omitted verb, i.e., "Remember, O Muhammad, when he said", and the meaning: "Will you not be wary of the punishment of Allah?"

Then He denounced them with His saying: ﴿Do you call upon Ba'l﴾. Ba'l is the name of an idol they used to worship, i.e., do you worship an idol and seek good from it?

Tha'lab said: People differed concerning His, glorified be He, saying "Ba'l". One group said: Ba'l here is the idol; another group said: Ba'l here is an angel; and Ibn Ishaq said: it is a woman they used to worship.

Al-Wahidi said: the exegetes say it means "lord" (rabban), and it is in the dialect of Yemen, where they call the master and the lord "ba'l".

Al-Nahhas said: both sayings are correct, i.e., do you call upon an idol that you made a lord ﴿and leave the best of creators﴾, i.e., and you abandon worshipping the best of those who are called "creator".

The noble name in His saying ﴿Allah, your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers of old﴾ is in the accusative as a substitution (badal) for "the best", and this is according to the reading of Hamza, al-Kisa'i, al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Yahya ibn Wathhab and al-A'mash, for they read all three names in the accusative. It was also said: the accusative is by way of praise (madh), and it was said: by way of explicative apposition ('atf al-bayan). Abu 'Ubayd related that the accusative is by way of description (na't).

Al-Nahhas said: This is an error; it is rather a substitution, and description is not permissible because it is not an ornamental qualifier. Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred this reading.

Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, 'Asim, Abu Ja'far, Shayba and Nafi' read in the nominative.

Abu Hatim said: with the meaning "He is Allah, your Lord." Al-Nahhas said: the best that has been said is that it is a subject and predicate without any supposition or omission. It is related from al-Akhfash that the nominative is preferable and better. Ibn al-Anbari said: whoever reads in the nominative or the accusative does not stop at "the best of creators" as a complete pause, because Allah is an apposition for "the best of creators" in both readings, and the meaning is that He is your creator and the creator of those before you, so He is the one who deserves worship.

﴿But they denied him, so they will surely be brought forth﴾, i.e., because of their denial of him they will indeed be brought forth into punishment. It has already been mentioned that the unrestricted sense of "bringing forth" is specific to evil.

﴿Except the chosen servants of Allah﴾, i.e., those among his people who were believers in Him. It is read with a kasra and a fatha on the lam, as has preceded. The meaning on the reading with kasra is that they devoted themselves sincerely to Allah, and on the reading with fatha is that Allah selected them from among His servants. Its explanation has already been given.

﴿And We left for him among the later generations: "Peace be upon the family of Yasin"﴾. Nafi', Ibn 'Amir, al-A'raj and Shayba read "'ala Al Yasin" with "Al" construed to "Yasin", meaning "the family of Yasin." The rest read with a kasra on the hamza and a sakin on the lam, joined with "Yasin" — (p-1250) except al-Hasan, who read "al-Yasin" with the definite article attached to "Yasin." It was said: the intended meaning in all these readings is Ilyas, and upon this the salutation has fallen, but it is a non-Arabic name, and the Arabs vary greatly in these non-Arabic names and often alter them.

Ibn Jinni said: The Arabs play with non-Arabic names in a variety of ways; so "Yasin," "Ilyas," and "Ilyasin" are one and the same thing.

Al-Akhfash said: The Arabs name a man's people by the name of the outstanding man among them, so they say "al-Mahalibah," meaning they named every man among them after al-Muhallab. He said: On this basis, he named each man among them "al-Yasin."

Al-Farra' said: "al-Yasin" may be taken as a plural, so that his companions are included within his name.

Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said: its underlying form is "al-Yasiyin," with the two ya's of the relative construction deleted, as they are deleted in "al-Ash'arin" and "al-A'jamin."

Al-Farra' and Abu 'Ubayda preferred the reading of the majority, saying: "He did not say in any of the surahs 'upon the family of so-and-so'; rather the name came as it is, and 'al-Yasin' is the same, since it means Ilyas or Ilyas and his followers."

Al-Kalbi said: The intended meaning of "the family of Yasin" is the family of Muhammad.

Al-Wahidi said: This is far-fetched, because what follows it and what precedes it in the discourse does not indicate it.

The explanation of ﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the good-doers. Indeed, he was among Our believing servants﴾ has already been given in full.

﴿And indeed Lut was among the messengers﴾. The story of Lut has already been mentioned in full.

﴿When We delivered him and his family, all of them﴾. The temporal clause is connected to an omitted verb, which is "remember," and it is not correct for it to be connected to "the messengers," because he was not sent at the time of his deliverance.

﴿Except an old woman among those who remained behind﴾. It has already been stated that "al-ghabir" may mean "past" and may mean "remaining," so the meaning is: except an old woman among those who remained behind in the punishment, or among those who passed away and were destroyed.

﴿Then We destroyed the others﴾, i.e., We annihilated them with punishment. The meaning is that in his deliverance and that of his family all together, except the old woman, and the destruction of the rest of his people who did not believe in him, there is a clear proof of the establishment of his being one of the messengers.

﴿And indeed you pass by them in the morning﴾. With this He addressed the Arabs, or the people of Makkah specifically, i.e., you pass by their dwellings in which are the traces of punishment at morning time.

﴿And by night﴾. The meaning: you pass by their dwellings on your journey to Syria and your return from it, by day and by night. ﴿Will you not then reason?﴾ — regarding what you witness in their dwellings of the traces of Allah's punishment that descended upon them, for in that is a lesson for those who take heed and an admonition for those who reflect.

﴿And indeed Yunus was among the messengers﴾. Yunus is Dhu al-Nun, and he is the son of Matta.

The exegetes said: Yunus had promised his people punishment, and when the punishment was delayed from them, he went out from among them, intending the sea, and boarded a ship. By his going to the sea he was like one fleeing from his master, so he was described as a runaway (ibaq), and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿When he fled to the laden ship﴾. The origin of "ibaq" is fleeing from a master, but since his flight from his people was without the permission of his Lord, he was described by it.

Al-Mubarrad said: the interpretation of "abaqa" is "ba'ada," i.e., he went far away, and from this comes the saying "abd abiq" (a runaway slave).

The people of knowledge have differed on whether his prophethood was before the fish swallowed him or after. The meaning of "mashhun" is "filled."

﴿So he drew lots and was among the losers﴾. Al-musahama originally means contest, and it is casting lots, which is that the arrow falls upon the one who loses. Al-Mubarrad said: i.e., he cast lots. He said: its origin is from the arrows that are shuffled. The meaning of ﴿was among the losers﴾ is that he became one of the defeated.

He said: It is said: "his argument was refuted (dahadat hujjatuhu), and Allah refuted it," and its origin is from slipping from the place of a grip. From this is the poet's saying:

"We slew the refuted ones in every ravine, and the eyes were cooled by their slaughter."

i.e., the defeated.

﴿Then the fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy﴾. It is said: "laqimtu al-luqmah" and "altaqamtuha" when I swallowed it, i.e., the fish swallowed him. The meaning of ﴿while he was blameworthy﴾ is that he was deserving of blame. It is said: "rajul mulim" when he does something for which he is blamed; but "malum" is one who is blamed whether or not he does what deserves blame. It was said: "mulim" means "faulted," from "alama al-rajul" when he did something by which he became faulted.

The meaning of this lottery is that when Yunus boarded the ship it was held back, so the sailors said: "Here is a slave who has run away from his master, and this is the custom of a ship: when there is a runaway in it, it does not sail." So they cast lots, and the lot fell upon Yunus, and he said: "I am the runaway," and he threw himself into the water.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: When they cast lots, a fish came to the ship with its mouth open, awaiting the command of its Lord, until when he threw himself into the water the fish seized him.

﴿Had he not been among those who glorify (Allah)﴾, i.e., those who remember Allah or those who pray to Him.

﴿He would have remained in its belly until the Day they are resurrected﴾, i.e., the belly of the fish would have been a grave for him until the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: he would have remained in its belly alive.

The exegetes differed on how long he remained in the belly of the fish. Al-Suddi, al-Kalbi and Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: forty days. Al-Dahhak said: twenty days. 'Ata' said: seven days. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: three days. It was also said: one hour.

In this verse there is encouragement to the remembrance of Allah and an invigoration for those who remember Him.

﴿So We cast him onto the open plain while he was ill﴾. Nabdh means to throw down.

Al-'Ara': Ibn al-A'rabi said: it is the desert. Al-Akhfash said: the open space. Abu 'Ubayda said: the wide expanse of land. Al-Farra' said: the empty place.

It is also related from Abu 'Ubayda that he said: it is the surface of the earth, and he recited for a man from Khuza'ah:

"I raised a leg whose stumbling I do not fear, and I cast my garments in the land of al-'ara'."

The meaning is that Allah threw him from the belly of the fish onto the wide desert where there is no vegetation, and he was ill at the time of his casting because of the harm he had suffered in the belly of the fish. It was said: his body became like the body of a child at birth.

Some exegetes found it problematic to reconcile what occurred here, His saying ﴿So We cast him onto the open plain﴾, with His saying elsewhere: ﴿Had it not been that a blessing from his Lord had overtaken him, he would have been cast onto the open plain while blameworthy﴾ [al-Qalam: 49], for this verse indicates that he was not cast onto the open plain.

Al-Nahhas and others answered: Allah, glorified be He, here informs that he was cast onto the open plain while not blameworthy, and had it not been for His mercy, mighty and majestic, he would have been cast onto the open plain while blameworthy.

﴿And We caused a gourd plant to grow over him﴾, i.e., a tree above him that shaded him. It was also said: the meaning of "over him" is "near him"; and it was said: the meaning of "over him" is "for him."

Al-yaqtin is the gourd plant. Al-Mubarrad said: "yaqtin" is said of every plant that has no stalk but spreads over the surface of the earth, like the gourd, the watermelon and the colocynth; but if it has a stalk that carries it, it is called simply a tree. This is the saying of al-Hasan, Muqatil and others.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is everything that grows and then dies within its year. Al-Jawhari said: al-yaqtin is the kind of tree that has no stem, like the gourd plant and similar plants.

Al-Zajjaj said: the derivation of al-yaqtin is from qatana bi-l-makan, meaning he stayed in the place, so it is on the pattern of yaf'il. It was also said that it is a non-Arabic word.

The exegetes (al-mufassirun) said: he would shelter from the sun under its shade. Allah appointed for him a doe from the wild animals, which would come to him morning and evening. He would drink from its milk until his flesh grew firm and his hair grew, and then Allah sent him after that. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more.﴾ They were his people, from whom he had fled to the sea, and what happened to him after his flight happened, as Allah related it to us in this surah. They were the people of Nineveh.

Qatada said: he was sent to the people of Nineveh, from the land of Mosul. The account of his story has already been discussed in full in the surah of Yunus. As for the "or" (aw) in ﴿or more﴾, it was said: it has the meaning of "and" (waw), so the meaning is: "and more."

Al-Farra' said: "or" (aw) here means "rather" (bal), and this is the view of Muqatil and al-Kalbi.

Al-Mubarrad, al-Zajjaj and al-Akhfash said: "or" here remains on its original meaning, and the meaning is: "or more, in your estimation, when one who sees them says: 'These are a hundred thousand or more.'" So the doubt entered only into the reporting of the words of the created beings.

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: they were more by twenty thousand. Al-Hasan said: by some thirty thousand. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: seventy thousand.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad read "wa-yazidun" without the alif of doubt.

Scholars of tafsir differed as to whether this sending mentioned here was the one that came before the fish swallowed him, so that the waw in "wa-arsalnahu" would be merely for joining what happened to him with the fish and his sending to his people, without regard to the order of what came first and what came later in the context. Or it is a sending after what happened to him with the fish, according to two views. We have already pointed to the disagreement among the scholars as to whether he had been sent before he fled from his people to the sea, or whether he was not sent until after that. The preferred view is that he was a messenger before he went to the sea, as is indicated by what we mentioned in the surah of Yunus, and he continued in the message. The sending mentioned here is after his prophethood and his messengership had already preceded.

﴿So they believed, and We gave them enjoyment for a time.﴾ That is: belief occurred from them after they had witnessed the signs of his prophethood, so Allah gave them enjoyment in this world until the end of their appointed terms and the limit of their lifespans.

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Asakir reported from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "Ilyas is Idris." Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir reported from Qatada something similar.

Ibn Mardawayh reported from Ibn Abbas that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Al-Khadir is Ilyas."

Al-Hakim, who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il, who declared it weak, reported from Anas, who said: "We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a journey. He halted at a stopping place, and there was a man in the valley saying: 'O Allah, make me one of the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), the merciful, the forgiven, the one who is rewarded by it.' I looked over the valley, and its length was eighty cubits or more. He said: 'Who are you?' I said: 'Anas, the servant of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' He said: 'Where is he?' I said: 'He is here, listening to your speech.' He said: 'Go to him, convey my greetings to him, and say to him: Your brother Ilyas sends you his greetings.' So I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him, and he came until he embraced him, and they sat talking. He said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, I only eat one day in each year, and this is the day of my breaking the fast, so eat with me.' Then a table was sent down to them from heaven: bread, fish and celery. They both ate, and they fed me, and they prayed the afternoon prayer. Then he bade him farewell, and then I saw him passing over the clouds toward the sky."

Al-Dhahabi, commenting on al-Hakim's authentication of it, said: "Rather it is fabricated; may Allah curse the one who fabricated it."

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir reported from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿Do you call upon Ba'l?﴾, that he said: "An idol."

Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh reported from him, regarding His words "Peace be upon the family of Yasin," that he said: "We are the family of Muhammad, the family of Yasin."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Allah sent Yunus to the people of his town, and they rejected what he brought them and refused it. When they did that, Allah revealed to them: 'I am sending upon them the punishment on such-and-such a day.' He was taken out from among them, and he informed his people of the punishment which Allah had promised to inflict upon them. They said: 'Watch him. If he leaves from among you, then by Allah, what he has promised you will certainly come.' When the night came in which they had been promised the punishment, and in its morning, he set out by night, and the people saw him and were wary, so they went out of the town into an open area of their land, and they separated every animal from its young. Then they cried out to Allah and turned in repentance, and they asked for pardon, and Allah pardoned them. Yunus waited for news of the town and its people until a passer-by came to him, and he said: 'What has become of the people of the town?' He said: 'When their prophet went out from among them, they knew that he had spoken truly about the punishment he had promised them, so they went out of their town into an open area, and then they separated every creature with young from its young, then they cried out to Allah and repented to Him, so He accepted from them and deferred the punishment from them.' Then Yunus said at that: 'I will never return to them as a liar, ever,' and he went off in his own direction." We have already discussed his story and what has been related about it in the surah of Yunus, so we will not repeat it.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi reported from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and he cast lots﴾, that he said: "He drew lots." ﴿And he was among those who were overcome﴾: "Those who lost the drawing."

Ibn Abi Shayba, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from him, regarding His words ﴿and he was blameworthy﴾, that he said: "Blameworthy: one who had done wrong."

Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Ahmad in al-Zuhd, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from him, regarding His words ﴿Had he not been one of those who glorify Allah﴾, that he said: "One of those who pray."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from him, regarding His words ﴿Had he not been one of those who glorify Allah﴾, that he said: "One of those who pray."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also reported from him, regarding His words ﴿So We cast him onto the open shore﴾, that he said: "We threw him onto the shore."

These same reporters also reported from him, regarding His words ﴿a gourd plant﴾, that he said: "The gourd."

Ibn Abi Shayba and Ibn al-Mundhir reported through the chain of Sa'id ibn Jubayr from him, who said: "Al-yaqtin is everything that spreads over the surface of the earth."

Ahmad in al-Zuhd, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh reported from him, who said: "The mission of Yunus was only after the fish had cast him out. Then he recited: ﴿So We cast him onto the open shore﴾ up to His words ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand﴾." It has already been mentioned from him what indicates that his mission was before that. And there is nothing in the verse that indicates what he mentioned, as we have already said.

al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh reported from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: "I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the words of Allah: ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more,﴾ and he said: 'They were more by twenty thousand.'" Al-Tirmidhi said: "Gharib (a narration found through only a single line of transmission)."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn Abbas, who said: "They were more by thirty thousand."

It is also reported from him that they were more by some thirty-odd thousand, and it is also reported from him that they were more by some forty thousand. There is not much benefit in the disagreement about this.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 37, verse 114–148 (part 1 of 2):

When He, glorified be He, finished mentioning the rescue of the sacrificed one (dhabih) from the slaughter, and the favour He bestowed upon him afterward in prophethood, He mentioned what He bestowed upon Musa and Harun, saying: ﴿And We certainly bestowed favour upon Musa and Harun﴾, meaning with prophethood and other great blessings with which Allah graced them both.

﴿And We delivered them and their people from the great distress﴾. By "their people" is meant the believers among the Children of Israel, and by "the great distress" is meant what they were in of the enslavement by Pharaoh and the afflictions that befell them from him. It was also said that it is the drowning that destroyed Pharaoh and his people, but the first is more apt.

﴿And We helped them﴾ came with the pronoun of the plural. Al-Farra' said: the pronoun refers to Musa, Harun and their people, because before it is ﴿and We delivered them and their people﴾. The meaning of "help" is support for them against their enemy, so that by that means they became ﴿the victorious﴾ over their enemy, after they had been under their subjugation and domination. It was also said that the pronoun in "We helped them" refers to the two, Musa and Harun, as an honouring of them both, but the first is more apt.

﴿And We gave them both the clear Book﴾. By "the Book" is meant the Torah. Al-Mustabin means the clear and manifest; it is said: "istabana kadha", i.e., it became clear.

﴿And We guided them both to the straight path﴾, i.e., the upright, with no crookedness in it, and it is the religion of Islam, for it is the path that leads to the sought goal.

﴿And We left for them both among the later generations: "Peace be upon Musa and Harun"﴾, i.e., We preserved for them both among the later nations the good praise. We have already discussed the matter of "peace" and the grammatical reason for its being in the nominative case, and likewise its explanation has preceded.

﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the good-doers. Indeed, they both were among Our believing servants﴾ — this was explained in this surah.

﴿And indeed Ilyas was among the messengers﴾. The exegetes said: he was a prophet of the prophets of the Children of Israel, and his story with his people is well known. It was said: he is Ilyas son of Yasin, of the lineage of Harun, brother of Musa.

Ibn Ishaq and others said: Ilyas was the one in charge of the affairs of the Children of Israel after Yusha', and it was said: he is Idris, but the first is more apt.

The majority read "Ilyas" with a hamza of kasra that is cut (i.e., a separate hamza, qat'), and Ibn Dhakwan read it with a connected hamza (wasl), and this reading is narrated from Ibn 'Amir. Ibn Mas'ud, al-A'mash and Yahya ibn Wathhab read "wa-inna Idris la-mina al-mursalin". Ubayy read "wa-inna Iyilis" with a kasra-marked hamza, then a sakin ya', then a kasra-marked lam, then a sakin ya', then an unpointed sin with a fatha.

﴿When he said to his people: "Will you not be wary of God?"﴾. It is a temporal clause (zarf) governed by his saying "among the messengers", or it is connected to an omitted verb, i.e., "Remember, O Muhammad, when he said", and the meaning: "Will you not be wary of the punishment of Allah?"

Then He denounced them with His saying: ﴿Do you call upon Ba'l﴾. Ba'l is the name of an idol they used to worship, i.e., do you worship an idol and seek good from it?

Tha'lab said: People differed concerning His, glorified be He, saying "Ba'l". One group said: Ba'l here is the idol; another group said: Ba'l here is an angel; and Ibn Ishaq said: it is a woman they used to worship.

Al-Wahidi said: the exegetes say it means "lord" (rabban), and it is in the dialect of Yemen, where they call the master and the lord "ba'l".

Al-Nahhas said: both sayings are correct, i.e., do you call upon an idol that you made a lord ﴿and leave the best of creators﴾, i.e., and you abandon worshipping the best of those who are called "creator".

The noble name in His saying ﴿Allah, your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers of old﴾ is in the accusative as a substitution (badal) for "the best", and this is according to the reading of Hamza, al-Kisa'i, al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Yahya ibn Wathhab and al-A'mash, for they read all three names in the accusative. It was also said: the accusative is by way of praise (madh), and it was said: by way of explicative apposition ('atf al-bayan). Abu 'Ubayd related that the accusative is by way of description (na't).

Al-Nahhas said: This is an error; it is rather a substitution, and description is not permissible because it is not an ornamental qualifier. Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred this reading.

Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, 'Asim, Abu Ja'far, Shayba and Nafi' read in the nominative.

Abu Hatim said: with the meaning "He is Allah, your Lord." Al-Nahhas said: the best that has been said is that it is a subject and predicate without any supposition or omission. It is related from al-Akhfash that the nominative is preferable and better. Ibn al-Anbari said: whoever reads in the nominative or the accusative does not stop at "the best of creators" as a complete pause, because Allah is an apposition for "the best of creators" in both readings, and the meaning is that He is your creator and the creator of those before you, so He is the one who deserves worship.

﴿But they denied him, so they will surely be brought forth﴾, i.e., because of their denial of him they will indeed be brought forth into punishment. It has already been mentioned that the unrestricted sense of "bringing forth" is specific to evil.

﴿Except the chosen servants of Allah﴾, i.e., those among his people who were believers in Him. It is read with a kasra and a fatha on the lam, as has preceded. The meaning on the reading with kasra is that they devoted themselves sincerely to Allah, and on the reading with fatha is that Allah selected them from among His servants. Its explanation has already been given.

﴿And We left for him among the later generations: "Peace be upon the family of Yasin"﴾. Nafi', Ibn 'Amir, al-A'raj and Shayba read "'ala Al Yasin" with "Al" construed to "Yasin", meaning "the family of Yasin." The rest read with a kasra on the hamza and a sakin on the lam, joined with "Yasin" — (p-1250) except al-Hasan, who read "al-Yasin" with the definite article attached to "Yasin." It was said: the intended meaning in all these readings is Ilyas, and upon this the salutation has fallen, but it is a non-Arabic name, and the Arabs vary greatly in these non-Arabic names and often alter them.

Ibn Jinni said: The Arabs play with non-Arabic names in a variety of ways; so "Yasin," "Ilyas," and "Ilyasin" are one and the same thing.

Al-Akhfash said: The Arabs name a man's people by the name of the outstanding man among them, so they say "al-Mahalibah," meaning they named every man among them after al-Muhallab. He said: On this basis, he named each man among them "al-Yasin."

Al-Farra' said: "al-Yasin" may be taken as a plural, so that his companions are included within his name.

Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said: its underlying form is "al-Yasiyin," with the two ya's of the relative construction deleted, as they are deleted in "al-Ash'arin" and "al-A'jamin."

Al-Farra' and Abu 'Ubayda preferred the reading of the majority, saying: "He did not say in any of the surahs 'upon the family of so-and-so'; rather the name came as it is, and 'al-Yasin' is the same, since it means Ilyas or Ilyas and his followers."

Al-Kalbi said: The intended meaning of "the family of Yasin" is the family of Muhammad.

Al-Wahidi said: This is far-fetched, because what follows it and what precedes it in the discourse does not indicate it.

The explanation of ﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the good-doers. Indeed, he was among Our believing servants﴾ has already been given in full.

﴿And indeed Lut was among the messengers﴾. The story of Lut has already been mentioned in full.

﴿When We delivered him and his family, all of them﴾. The temporal clause is connected to an omitted verb, which is "remember," and it is not correct for it to be connected to "the messengers," because he was not sent at the time of his deliverance.

﴿Except an old woman among those who remained behind﴾. It has already been stated that "al-ghabir" may mean "past" and may mean "remaining," so the meaning is: except an old woman among those who remained behind in the punishment, or among those who passed away and were destroyed.

﴿Then We destroyed the others﴾, i.e., We annihilated them with punishment. The meaning is that in his deliverance and that of his family all together, except the old woman, and the destruction of the rest of his people who did not believe in him, there is a clear proof of the establishment of his being one of the messengers.

﴿And indeed you pass by them in the morning﴾. With this He addressed the Arabs, or the people of Makkah specifically, i.e., you pass by their dwellings in which are the traces of punishment at morning time.

﴿And by night﴾. The meaning: you pass by their dwellings on your journey to Syria and your return from it, by day and by night. ﴿Will you not then reason?﴾ — regarding what you witness in their dwellings of the traces of Allah's punishment that descended upon them, for in that is a lesson for those who take heed and an admonition for those who reflect.

﴿And indeed Yunus was among the messengers﴾. Yunus is Dhu al-Nun, and he is the son of Matta.

The exegetes said: Yunus had promised his people punishment, and when the punishment was delayed from them, he went out from among them, intending the sea, and boarded a ship. By his going to the sea he was like one fleeing from his master, so he was described as a runaway (ibaq), and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿When he fled to the laden ship﴾. The origin of "ibaq" is fleeing from a master, but since his flight from his people was without the permission of his Lord, he was described by it.

Al-Mubarrad said: the interpretation of "abaqa" is "ba'ada," i.e., he went far away, and from this comes the saying "abd abiq" (a runaway slave).

The people of knowledge have differed on whether his prophethood was before the fish swallowed him or after. The meaning of "mashhun" is "filled."

﴿So he drew lots and was among the losers﴾. Al-musahama originally means contest, and it is casting lots, which is that the arrow falls upon the one who loses. Al-Mubarrad said: i.e., he cast lots. He said: its origin is from the arrows that are shuffled. The meaning of ﴿was among the losers﴾ is that he became one of the defeated.

He said: It is said: "his argument was refuted (dahadat hujjatuhu), and Allah refuted it," and its origin is from slipping from the place of a grip. From this is the poet's saying:

"We slew the refuted ones in every ravine, and the eyes were cooled by their slaughter."

i.e., the defeated.

﴿Then the fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy﴾. It is said: "laqimtu al-luqmah" and "altaqamtuha" when I swallowed it, i.e., the fish swallowed him. The meaning of ﴿while he was blameworthy﴾ is that he was deserving of blame. It is said: "rajul mulim" when he does something for which he is blamed; but "malum" is one who is blamed whether or not he does what deserves blame. It was said: "mulim" means "faulted," from "alama al-rajul" when he did something by which he became faulted.

The meaning of this lottery is that when Yunus boarded the ship it was held back, so the sailors said: "Here is a slave who has run away from his master, and this is the custom of a ship: when there is a runaway in it, it does not sail." So they cast lots, and the lot fell upon Yunus, and he said: "I am the runaway," and he threw himself into the water.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: When they cast lots, a fish came to the ship with its mouth open, awaiting the command of its Lord, until when he threw himself into the water the fish seized him.

﴿Had he not been among those who glorify (Allah)﴾, i.e., those who remember Allah or those who pray to Him.

﴿He would have remained in its belly until the Day they are resurrected﴾, i.e., the belly of the fish would have been a grave for him until the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: he would have remained in its belly alive.

The exegetes differed on how long he remained in the belly of the fish. Al-Suddi, al-Kalbi and Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: forty days. Al-Dahhak said: twenty days. 'Ata' said: seven days. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: three days. It was also said: one hour.

In this verse there is encouragement to the remembrance of Allah and an invigoration for those who remember Him.

﴿So We cast him onto the open plain while he was ill﴾. Nabdh means to throw down.

Al-'Ara': Ibn al-A'rabi said: it is the desert. Al-Akhfash said: the open space. Abu 'Ubayda said: the wide expanse of land. Al-Farra' said: the empty place.

It is also related from Abu 'Ubayda that he said: it is the surface of the earth, and he recited for a man from Khuza'ah:

"I raised a leg whose stumbling I do not fear, and I cast my garments in the land of al-'ara'."

The meaning is that Allah threw him from the belly of the fish onto the wide desert where there is no vegetation, and he was ill at the time of his casting because of the harm he had suffered in the belly of the fish. It was said: his body became like the body of a child at birth.

Some exegetes found it problematic to reconcile what occurred here, His saying ﴿So We cast him onto the open plain﴾, with His saying elsewhere: ﴿Had it not been that a blessing from his Lord had overtaken him, he would have been cast onto the open plain while blameworthy﴾ [al-Qalam: 49], for this verse indicates that he was not cast onto the open plain.

Al-Nahhas and others answered: Allah, glorified be He, here informs that he was cast onto the open plain while not blameworthy, and had it not been for His mercy, mighty and majestic, he would have been cast onto the open plain while blameworthy.

﴿And We caused a gourd plant to grow over him﴾, i.e., a tree above him that shaded him. It was also said: the meaning of "over him" is "near him"; and it was said: the meaning of "over him" is "for him."

Al-yaqtin is the gourd plant. Al-Mubarrad said: "yaqtin" is said of every plant that has no stalk but spreads over the surface of the earth, like the gourd, the watermelon and the colocynth; but if it has a stalk that carries it, it is called simply a tree. This is the saying of al-Hasan, Muqatil and others.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is everything that grows and then dies within its year. Al-Jawhari said: al-yaqtin is the kind of tree that has no stem, like the gourd plant and similar plants.

Al-Zajjaj said: the derivation of al-yaqtin is from qatana bi-l-makan, meaning he stayed in the place, so it is on the pattern of yaf'il. It was also said that it is a non-Arabic word.

The exegetes (al-mufassirun) said: he would shelter from the sun under its shade. Allah appointed for him a doe from the wild animals, which would come to him morning and evening. He would drink from its milk until his flesh grew firm and his hair grew, and then Allah sent him after that. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more.﴾ They were his people, from whom he had fled to the sea, and what happened to him after his flight happened, as Allah related it to us in this surah. They were the people of Nineveh.

Qatada said: he was sent to the people of Nineveh, from the land of Mosul. The account of his story has already been discussed in full in the surah of Yunus. As for the "or" (aw) in ﴿or more﴾, it was said: it has the meaning of "and" (waw), so the meaning is: "and more."

Al-Farra' said: "or" (aw) here means "rather" (bal), and this is the view of Muqatil and al-Kalbi.

Al-Mubarrad, al-Zajjaj and al-Akhfash said: "or" here remains on its original meaning, and the meaning is: "or more, in your estimation, when one who sees them says: 'These are a hundred thousand or more.'" So the doubt entered only into the reporting of the words of the created beings.

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: they were more by twenty thousand. Al-Hasan said: by some thirty thousand. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: seventy thousand.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad read "wa-yazidun" without the alif of doubt.

Scholars of tafsir differed as to whether this sending mentioned here was the one that came before the fish swallowed him, so that the waw in "wa-arsalnahu" would be merely for joining what happened to him with the fish and his sending to his people, without regard to the order of what came first and what came later in the context. Or it is a sending after what happened to him with the fish, according to two views. We have already pointed to the disagreement among the scholars as to whether he had been sent before he fled from his people to the sea, or whether he was not sent until after that. The preferred view is that he was a messenger before he went to the sea, as is indicated by what we mentioned in the surah of Yunus, and he continued in the message. The sending mentioned here is after his prophethood and his messengership had already preceded.

﴿So they believed, and We gave them enjoyment for a time.﴾ That is: belief occurred from them after they had witnessed the signs of his prophethood, so Allah gave them enjoyment in this world until the end of their appointed terms and the limit of their lifespans.

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Asakir reported from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "Ilyas is Idris." Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir reported from Qatada something similar.

Ibn Mardawayh reported from Ibn Abbas that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Al-Khadir is Ilyas."

Al-Hakim, who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il, who declared it weak, reported from Anas, who said: "We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a journey. He halted at a stopping place, and there was a man in the valley saying: 'O Allah, make me one of the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), the merciful, the forgiven, the one who is rewarded by it.' I looked over the valley, and its length was eighty cubits or more. He said: 'Who are you?' I said: 'Anas, the servant of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' He said: 'Where is he?' I said: 'He is here, listening to your speech.' He said: 'Go to him, convey my greetings to him, and say to him: Your brother Ilyas sends you his greetings.' So I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him, and he came until he embraced him, and they sat talking. He said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, I only eat one day in each year, and this is the day of my breaking the fast, so eat with me.' Then a table was sent down to them from heaven: bread, fish and celery. They both ate, and they fed me, and they prayed the afternoon prayer. Then he bade him farewell, and then I saw him passing over the clouds toward the sky."

Al-Dhahabi, commenting on al-Hakim's authentication of it, said: "Rather it is fabricated; may Allah curse the one who fabricated it."

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir reported from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿Do you call upon Ba'l?﴾, that he said: "An idol."

Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh reported from him, regarding His words "Peace be upon the family of Yasin," that he said: "We are the family of Muhammad, the family of Yasin."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Allah sent Yunus to the people of his town, and they rejected what he brought them and refused it. When they did that, Allah revealed to them: 'I am sending upon them the punishment on such-and-such a day.' He was taken out from among them, and he informed his people of the punishment which Allah had promised to inflict upon them. They said: 'Watch him. If he leaves from among you, then by Allah, what he has promised you will certainly come.' When the night came in which they had been promised the punishment, and in its morning, he set out by night, and the people saw him and were wary, so they went out of the town into an open area of their land, and they separated every animal from its young. Then they cried out to Allah and turned in repentance, and they asked for pardon, and Allah pardoned them. Yunus waited for news of the town and its people until a passer-by came to him, and he said: 'What has become of the people of the town?' He said: 'When their prophet went out from among them, they knew that he had spoken truly about the punishment he had promised them, so they went out of their town into an open area, and then they separated every creature with young from its young, then they cried out to Allah and repented to Him, so He accepted from them and deferred the punishment from them.' Then Yunus said at that: 'I will never return to them as a liar, ever,' and he went off in his own direction." We have already discussed his story and what has been related about it in the surah of Yunus, so we will not repeat it.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi reported from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and he cast lots﴾, that he said: "He drew lots." ﴿And he was among those who were overcome﴾: "Those who lost the drawing."

Ibn Abi Shayba, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from him, regarding His words ﴿and he was blameworthy﴾, that he said: "Blameworthy: one who had done wrong."

Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Ahmad in al-Zuhd, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from him, regarding His words ﴿Had he not been one of those who glorify Allah﴾, that he said: "One of those who pray."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from him, regarding His words ﴿Had he not been one of those who glorify Allah﴾, that he said: "One of those who pray."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also reported from him, regarding His words ﴿So We cast him onto the open shore﴾, that he said: "We threw him onto the shore."

These same reporters also reported from him, regarding His words ﴿a gourd plant﴾, that he said: "The gourd."

Ibn Abi Shayba and Ibn al-Mundhir reported through the chain of Sa'id ibn Jubayr from him, who said: "Al-yaqtin is everything that spreads over the surface of the earth."

Ahmad in al-Zuhd, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh reported from him, who said: "The mission of Yunus was only after the fish had cast him out. Then he recited: ﴿So We cast him onto the open shore﴾ up to His words ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand﴾." It has already been mentioned from him what indicates that his mission was before that. And there is nothing in the verse that indicates what he mentioned, as we have already said.

al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh reported from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: "I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the words of Allah: ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more,﴾ and he said: 'They were more by twenty thousand.'" Al-Tirmidhi said: "Gharib (a narration found through only a single line of transmission)."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn Abbas, who said: "They were more by thirty thousand."

It is also reported from him that they were more by some thirty-odd thousand, and it is also reported from him that they were more by some forty thousand. There is not much benefit in the disagreement about this.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 37, verse 114–148 (part 1 of 2):

When He, glorified be He, finished mentioning the rescue of the sacrificed one (dhabih) from the slaughter, and the favour He bestowed upon him afterward in prophethood, He mentioned what He bestowed upon Musa and Harun, saying: ﴿And We certainly bestowed favour upon Musa and Harun﴾, meaning with prophethood and other great blessings with which Allah graced them both.

﴿And We delivered them and their people from the great distress﴾. By "their people" is meant the believers among the Children of Israel, and by "the great distress" is meant what they were in of the enslavement by Pharaoh and the afflictions that befell them from him. It was also said that it is the drowning that destroyed Pharaoh and his people, but the first is more apt.

﴿And We helped them﴾ came with the pronoun of the plural. Al-Farra' said: the pronoun refers to Musa, Harun and their people, because before it is ﴿and We delivered them and their people﴾. The meaning of "help" is support for them against their enemy, so that by that means they became ﴿the victorious﴾ over their enemy, after they had been under their subjugation and domination. It was also said that the pronoun in "We helped them" refers to the two, Musa and Harun, as an honouring of them both, but the first is more apt.

﴿And We gave them both the clear Book﴾. By "the Book" is meant the Torah. Al-Mustabin means the clear and manifest; it is said: "istabana kadha", i.e., it became clear.

﴿And We guided them both to the straight path﴾, i.e., the upright, with no crookedness in it, and it is the religion of Islam, for it is the path that leads to the sought goal.

﴿And We left for them both among the later generations: "Peace be upon Musa and Harun"﴾, i.e., We preserved for them both among the later nations the good praise. We have already discussed the matter of "peace" and the grammatical reason for its being in the nominative case, and likewise its explanation has preceded.

﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the good-doers. Indeed, they both were among Our believing servants﴾ — this was explained in this surah.

﴿And indeed Ilyas was among the messengers﴾. The exegetes said: he was a prophet of the prophets of the Children of Israel, and his story with his people is well known. It was said: he is Ilyas son of Yasin, of the lineage of Harun, brother of Musa.

Ibn Ishaq and others said: Ilyas was the one in charge of the affairs of the Children of Israel after Yusha', and it was said: he is Idris, but the first is more apt.

The majority read "Ilyas" with a hamza of kasra that is cut (i.e., a separate hamza, qat'), and Ibn Dhakwan read it with a connected hamza (wasl), and this reading is narrated from Ibn 'Amir. Ibn Mas'ud, al-A'mash and Yahya ibn Wathhab read "wa-inna Idris la-mina al-mursalin". Ubayy read "wa-inna Iyilis" with a kasra-marked hamza, then a sakin ya', then a kasra-marked lam, then a sakin ya', then an unpointed sin with a fatha.

﴿When he said to his people: "Will you not be wary of God?"﴾. It is a temporal clause (zarf) governed by his saying "among the messengers", or it is connected to an omitted verb, i.e., "Remember, O Muhammad, when he said", and the meaning: "Will you not be wary of the punishment of Allah?"

Then He denounced them with His saying: ﴿Do you call upon Ba'l﴾. Ba'l is the name of an idol they used to worship, i.e., do you worship an idol and seek good from it?

Tha'lab said: People differed concerning His, glorified be He, saying "Ba'l". One group said: Ba'l here is the idol; another group said: Ba'l here is an angel; and Ibn Ishaq said: it is a woman they used to worship.

Al-Wahidi said: the exegetes say it means "lord" (rabban), and it is in the dialect of Yemen, where they call the master and the lord "ba'l".

Al-Nahhas said: both sayings are correct, i.e., do you call upon an idol that you made a lord ﴿and leave the best of creators﴾, i.e., and you abandon worshipping the best of those who are called "creator".

The noble name in His saying ﴿Allah, your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers of old﴾ is in the accusative as a substitution (badal) for "the best", and this is according to the reading of Hamza, al-Kisa'i, al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Yahya ibn Wathhab and al-A'mash, for they read all three names in the accusative. It was also said: the accusative is by way of praise (madh), and it was said: by way of explicative apposition ('atf al-bayan). Abu 'Ubayd related that the accusative is by way of description (na't).

Al-Nahhas said: This is an error; it is rather a substitution, and description is not permissible because it is not an ornamental qualifier. Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred this reading.

Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, 'Asim, Abu Ja'far, Shayba and Nafi' read in the nominative.

Abu Hatim said: with the meaning "He is Allah, your Lord." Al-Nahhas said: the best that has been said is that it is a subject and predicate without any supposition or omission. It is related from al-Akhfash that the nominative is preferable and better. Ibn al-Anbari said: whoever reads in the nominative or the accusative does not stop at "the best of creators" as a complete pause, because Allah is an apposition for "the best of creators" in both readings, and the meaning is that He is your creator and the creator of those before you, so He is the one who deserves worship.

﴿But they denied him, so they will surely be brought forth﴾, i.e., because of their denial of him they will indeed be brought forth into punishment. It has already been mentioned that the unrestricted sense of "bringing forth" is specific to evil.

﴿Except the chosen servants of Allah﴾, i.e., those among his people who were believers in Him. It is read with a kasra and a fatha on the lam, as has preceded. The meaning on the reading with kasra is that they devoted themselves sincerely to Allah, and on the reading with fatha is that Allah selected them from among His servants. Its explanation has already been given.

﴿And We left for him among the later generations: "Peace be upon the family of Yasin"﴾. Nafi', Ibn 'Amir, al-A'raj and Shayba read "'ala Al Yasin" with "Al" construed to "Yasin", meaning "the family of Yasin." The rest read with a kasra on the hamza and a sakin on the lam, joined with "Yasin" — (p-1250) except al-Hasan, who read "al-Yasin" with the definite article attached to "Yasin." It was said: the intended meaning in all these readings is Ilyas, and upon this the salutation has fallen, but it is a non-Arabic name, and the Arabs vary greatly in these non-Arabic names and often alter them.

Ibn Jinni said: The Arabs play with non-Arabic names in a variety of ways; so "Yasin," "Ilyas," and "Ilyasin" are one and the same thing.

Al-Akhfash said: The Arabs name a man's people by the name of the outstanding man among them, so they say "al-Mahalibah," meaning they named every man among them after al-Muhallab. He said: On this basis, he named each man among them "al-Yasin."

Al-Farra' said: "al-Yasin" may be taken as a plural, so that his companions are included within his name.

Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said: its underlying form is "al-Yasiyin," with the two ya's of the relative construction deleted, as they are deleted in "al-Ash'arin" and "al-A'jamin."

Al-Farra' and Abu 'Ubayda preferred the reading of the majority, saying: "He did not say in any of the surahs 'upon the family of so-and-so'; rather the name came as it is, and 'al-Yasin' is the same, since it means Ilyas or Ilyas and his followers."

Al-Kalbi said: The intended meaning of "the family of Yasin" is the family of Muhammad.

Al-Wahidi said: This is far-fetched, because what follows it and what precedes it in the discourse does not indicate it.

The explanation of ﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the good-doers. Indeed, he was among Our believing servants﴾ has already been given in full.

﴿And indeed Lut was among the messengers﴾. The story of Lut has already been mentioned in full.

﴿When We delivered him and his family, all of them﴾. The temporal clause is connected to an omitted verb, which is "remember," and it is not correct for it to be connected to "the messengers," because he was not sent at the time of his deliverance.

﴿Except an old woman among those who remained behind﴾. It has already been stated that "al-ghabir" may mean "past" and may mean "remaining," so the meaning is: except an old woman among those who remained behind in the punishment, or among those who passed away and were destroyed.

﴿Then We destroyed the others﴾, i.e., We annihilated them with punishment. The meaning is that in his deliverance and that of his family all together, except the old woman, and the destruction of the rest of his people who did not believe in him, there is a clear proof of the establishment of his being one of the messengers.

﴿And indeed you pass by them in the morning﴾. With this He addressed the Arabs, or the people of Makkah specifically, i.e., you pass by their dwellings in which are the traces of punishment at morning time.

﴿And by night﴾. The meaning: you pass by their dwellings on your journey to Syria and your return from it, by day and by night. ﴿Will you not then reason?﴾ — regarding what you witness in their dwellings of the traces of Allah's punishment that descended upon them, for in that is a lesson for those who take heed and an admonition for those who reflect.

﴿And indeed Yunus was among the messengers﴾. Yunus is Dhu al-Nun, and he is the son of Matta.

The exegetes said: Yunus had promised his people punishment, and when the punishment was delayed from them, he went out from among them, intending the sea, and boarded a ship. By his going to the sea he was like one fleeing from his master, so he was described as a runaway (ibaq), and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿When he fled to the laden ship﴾. The origin of "ibaq" is fleeing from a master, but since his flight from his people was without the permission of his Lord, he was described by it.

Al-Mubarrad said: the interpretation of "abaqa" is "ba'ada," i.e., he went far away, and from this comes the saying "abd abiq" (a runaway slave).

The people of knowledge have differed on whether his prophethood was before the fish swallowed him or after. The meaning of "mashhun" is "filled."

﴿So he drew lots and was among the losers﴾. Al-musahama originally means contest, and it is casting lots, which is that the arrow falls upon the one who loses. Al-Mubarrad said: i.e., he cast lots. He said: its origin is from the arrows that are shuffled. The meaning of ﴿was among the losers﴾ is that he became one of the defeated.

He said: It is said: "his argument was refuted (dahadat hujjatuhu), and Allah refuted it," and its origin is from slipping from the place of a grip. From this is the poet's saying:

"We slew the refuted ones in every ravine, and the eyes were cooled by their slaughter."

i.e., the defeated.

﴿Then the fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy﴾. It is said: "laqimtu al-luqmah" and "altaqamtuha" when I swallowed it, i.e., the fish swallowed him. The meaning of ﴿while he was blameworthy﴾ is that he was deserving of blame. It is said: "rajul mulim" when he does something for which he is blamed; but "malum" is one who is blamed whether or not he does what deserves blame. It was said: "mulim" means "faulted," from "alama al-rajul" when he did something by which he became faulted.

The meaning of this lottery is that when Yunus boarded the ship it was held back, so the sailors said: "Here is a slave who has run away from his master, and this is the custom of a ship: when there is a runaway in it, it does not sail." So they cast lots, and the lot fell upon Yunus, and he said: "I am the runaway," and he threw himself into the water.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: When they cast lots, a fish came to the ship with its mouth open, awaiting the command of its Lord, until when he threw himself into the water the fish seized him.

﴿Had he not been among those who glorify (Allah)﴾, i.e., those who remember Allah or those who pray to Him.

﴿He would have remained in its belly until the Day they are resurrected﴾, i.e., the belly of the fish would have been a grave for him until the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: he would have remained in its belly alive.

The exegetes differed on how long he remained in the belly of the fish. Al-Suddi, al-Kalbi and Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: forty days. Al-Dahhak said: twenty days. 'Ata' said: seven days. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: three days. It was also said: one hour.

In this verse there is encouragement to the remembrance of Allah and an invigoration for those who remember Him.

﴿So We cast him onto the open plain while he was ill﴾. Nabdh means to throw down.

Al-'Ara': Ibn al-A'rabi said: it is the desert. Al-Akhfash said: the open space. Abu 'Ubayda said: the wide expanse of land. Al-Farra' said: the empty place.

It is also related from Abu 'Ubayda that he said: it is the surface of the earth, and he recited for a man from Khuza'ah:

"I raised a leg whose stumbling I do not fear, and I cast my garments in the land of al-'ara'."
